policy_title: Acupuncture for Chronic Lower Back Pain

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement guidelines, for 2022 and later, for the Medicare Part B benefit for acupuncture for chronic lower back pain (cLBP). Note: Some Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans have a supplemental benefit that covers acupuncture services that Original Medicare would not cover. This policy does not apply to services provided under one of those benefits.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana MA plans cover dry needling and acupuncture services under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit for the same diagnoses as Original Medicare. Except where noted below, providers must report acupuncture for cLBP services consistent with guidance in applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published transmittals and Internet-only Manuals. Except where noted below, Humana MA plans allow acupuncture for cLBP services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service.

extracted_content.title: Practitioner Type
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Practitioner Type
extracted_content.content: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2022, Humana MA plans’ acupuncture for cLBP benefit is not limited to services provided only by practitioner types that can provide services under Original Medicare’s acupuncture coverage. Instead, Humana MA plans permit practitioners who satisfy all applicable acupuncture licensure and plan requirements, such as plan participation requirements, to submit claims for services for acupuncture for cLBP.

extracted_content.title: Number of Sessions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Number of Sessions
extracted_content.content: Humana treats all services covered under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit furnished the same day as if they were furnished in one session. For 2022 and later, Humana MA plans cover up to 20 sessions per year. Therefore, Humana MA plans do not require providers to report modifier KX for charges for acupuncture visits 13 through 20 in any calendar year, despite CMS acupuncture billing guidance, for Original Medicare, about modifier KX billing. Note: For 2022 through 2025, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient’s primary care provider (PCP). For 2026, whether the 20-session limitation applies to services rendered by the patient’s PCP varies by plan as follows: • For Humana Group MA plans, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient’s PCP. • For Humana Individual MA plans, the 20-session limitation does apply to services rendered by the patient’s PCP.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: An ambulance is a professionally operated vehicle, provided by a licensed ambulance service, equipped for the transportation of a sick or injured person to or from the nearest medical facility qualified to treat the person's sickness or bodily injury. This policy establishes Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for ambulance services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow medically necessary ground ambulance and fixed or rotary wing air ambulance services according to Original Medicare guidelines. Humana only reimburses for covered transportation and mileage charges. The amount allowed for transportation includes reimbursement for all other items and services provided. Humana does not make separate payment for such items and services, including but not limited to oxygen, drugs, extra attendants, supplies, electrocardiograms (ECG or EKG) and night differential. Ambulance transportation provided to a member while registered as an inpatient at a hospital or skilled nursing facility (SNF), if billed, must be included in the facility’s related consolidated inpatient claim. Charges for transportation of an inpatient will only be considered for reimbursement within the adjudication of the inpatient stay itself. In some situations, Humana determines that, though transportation was medically necessary, the mode of transportation may not have been medically necessary, such as transportation by air. When Humana determines that transportation was medically necessary, but air transportation was not medically necessary, Humana allows ground ambulance rates for the transportation. Generally, reimbursement for ambulance mileage to a facility is limited to the distance from the place from which the patient was transported to the nearest appropriate facility. However, when Humana authorizes admission to a facility in advance, regardless of whether prior authorization is required, Humana reimburses for mileage for the related ambulance transportation to that facility. A provider should bill all of the coverable mileage with HCPCS code A0425, A0435 or A0436 . However, if a provider bills such mileage with HCPCS code A0888 , Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. If the facility did not obtain prior authorization from Humana for the related admission, a provider should bill mileage for transportation beyond the closest facility with HCPCS code A0888 . Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. Humana adjusts reimbursement of covered transportation and mileage charges when multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, indicated by modifier GM . If two patients are transported, Humana allows 75 percent of the provider’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and 50 percent of the provider’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage. If three patients are transported, Humana allows 60 percent of the provider’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and a prorated percent of the provider’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage, based on the number of patients on board. Note : Some Humana MA plans have supplemental transportation benefits, which provide coverage of some transportation services that Original Medicare would not cover. Providers and members are advised to contact Humana to verify if a Humana MA plan has supplemental transportation benefits.

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Providers must bill appropriate modifiers with ambulance charges. Ambulance origin and destination modifiers are billed with both the transportation and mileage charges. When reporting ambulance origin and destination modifiers , the first letter represents the place of origin, and the second letter represents the destination. If a patient is pronounced dead after the ambulance is dispatched but before being loaded on board, providers must report modifier QL with the transportation charge rather than ambulance origin and destination modifiers . In such circumstances, mileage is not

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: covered. However, if providers report the mileage charge, it must be billed with modifier QL , and it is not reimbursed. If multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, providers must report modifier GM with the transportation and mileage charges. Providers must bill the ZIP code of the point of pickup (POP). For transportation for less than 100 miles, ambulance mileage may be reported in fractional units to the nearest tenth of a mile. When more than one hospital-to-hospital ambulance service is provided on the same day, the provider must submit a charge for each segment of transportation on a separate claim line with a unit of 1.

extracted_content.title: Additional provision for out-of-network providers
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Additional provision for out-of-network providers
extracted_content.content: 42 CFR 422.214 requires an out-of-network provider to accept, as payment in full, the amount the provider could collect if the patient were enrolled in Original Medicare. The provider can collect from the MA plan member the cost-sharing amount required under the MA plan and collect the remainder of the allowed amount from the MA plan.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for anesthesia services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional services only.

extracted_content.title: Reporting Anesthesia Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Reporting Anesthesia Services
extracted_content.content: Humana requires anesthesia services to be reported using a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code in the 00100 – 01999 range.

extracted_content.title: Anesthesia Reimbursement Calculation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Anesthesia Reimbursement Calculation
extracted_content.content: Humana plans calculate the reimbursement of anesthesia services with consideration to the base value units for the procedure, time units, modifiers and the conversion factor. The formula is as follows: (CMS Base Value Unit + Time Units + Anesthesia Physical Status Modifier Unit, if applicable) x Conversion Factor = Anesthesia Allowable. Note: Some anesthesia services are not time-based; therefore, this calculation does not apply to such services.

extracted_content.title: Reporting Anesthesia Time
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Reporting Anesthesia Time
extracted_content.content: Humana requires actual anesthesia time to be reported in one-minute increments in the anesthesia minutes field. Note: Some anesthesia services are not time-based and are excluded from this requirement.

extracted_content.title: Common Modifiers for Anesthesia Claims
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Common Modifiers for Anesthesia Claims
extracted_content.content: Humana requires the anesthesia service code to be appended, as appropriate, with modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ. For an allowed anesthesia charge submitted with modifiers AA, QK, QX, QY or QZ , Humana plans allow the following percentage of the provider’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan : Note: Reimbursement of an anesthesia charge shall not exceed 100 percent of the total amount allowed for a single service reported on multiple providers’ claims, such as when an anesthesiologist directs a nonphysician anesthetist. Additionally, for any coverable single anesthesia service, Humana plans allow no more than one anesthesiologist charge and allow no more than one nonphysician anesthetist charge. Humana calculates the reimbursement of an allowed anesthesia charge submitted with modifier AD with three base units, regardless of the base value units of the procedure code, multiplied by the conversion factor. One additional unit is considered when documentation confirms the supervising physician was present at induction. Additional units for length of time, qualifying circumstances codes or physical status modifiers are not allowed. Monitored anesthesia care must be indicated using modifier G8, G9 or QS , with the monitored anesthesia care modifier reported after modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ .

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement for Post-Operative Pain Management Procedures
extracted_content.subsection: Reimbursement for Post-Operative Pain Management Procedures
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Reimbursement for Post-Operative Pain Management Procedures
extracted_content.content: A medically necessary anesthesia procedure, such as an epidural injection or nerve block, administered with the intent to manage post-operative pain, may be reimbursed separately when the adequacy of the intra-operative anesthesia is not dependent on the epidural injection or nerve block. All the following requirements must be satisfied to qualify for separate reimbursement from the intra-operative anesthesia: • Medical record documentation of the post-operative pain management procedure must: – Be separate from the anesthesia record – Confirm the procedure was for post-operative pain management and the adequacy of the intra-operative anesthesia is not dependent on the epidural injection or nerve block – Include details about the procedure itself – Confirm the surgeon requested the anesthetist administer the procedure – Confirm the patient consented to the post-operative pain management plan and procedure • The time spent placing or administering a post-operative pain management procedure cannot be included in the intra-operative anesthesia time. • Modifier 59, XE or XU must be appended to the post-operative pain management procedure code to indicate a distinct procedural service was performed. • Post-operative pain management procedures may be administered pre-operatively, intra-operatively or post-operatively. Post-operative pain management procedures are not separately reimbursed when reported by the same physician reporting the procedure or surgical charge.

extracted_content.title: Additional Reporting and Reimbursement Considerations
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Additional Reporting and Reimbursement Considerations
extracted_content.content: In certain circumstances additional payment rules may apply, including but not limited to the following: • When multiple procedures are performed on the same patient during a single anesthesia session, only the anesthesia service code with the highest base unit value should be reported. The combined time for all procedures should be reported with that code. • Humana plans do not reimburse for anesthesia services reported by the attending surgeon.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), assistant at surgery services are those services rendered by physicians or nonphysician practitioners (NPPs) who actively assist the physician in charge of performing a surgical procedure.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

extracted_content.title: Coverage
extracted_content.content: Original Medicare (OM) covers an assistant at surgery service provided by a physician, with some exclusions, or an NPP. A charge for an assistant at surgery service provided by another individual is not payable. Therefore, a Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plan denies, to provider liability, a charge for an assistant at surgery service submitted by an individual whose service would not be coverable for an enrollee of OM. Humana uses the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File assistant at surgery indicator to determine if an assistant at surgery is medically necessary and, therefore, covered. When the MPFS Relative Value File is not definitive, then Humana’s internal criteria are used.

extracted_content.title: Assistant at Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
extracted_content.subsection: Assistant at Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Assistant at Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
extracted_content.content: Humana determines coverage of a charge submitted by an assistant at surgery in a teaching hospital consistent with the qualifications required by CMS for an OM enrollee.

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Only one of the following modifiers should be billed per charge: AS, 80, 81 or 82 . An assistant at surgery should bill the same procedure code as the primary surgeon and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier, except when billing for assistance during a cesarean delivery. When billing for assistance only during a cesarean delivery, the assistant at surgery should bill Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code 59514 (cesarean delivery only) or CPT code 59620 (c esarean delivery only, following attempted vaginal delivery after previous cesarean delivery) and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier. Humana will not reimburse a practitioner who acts as an assistant at surgery in a cesarean delivery any more than the assistant at surgery rate that would apply for the CPT code appropriate for delivery only.

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement
extracted_content.content: A Humana MA plan allows an assistant at surgery physician charge, indicated by modifier 80, 81 or 82, at 16 percent of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan , subject to any other applicable reductions, for a service considered medically necessary. A Humana MA plan allows an assistant at surgery NPP charge, indicated by modifier AS , at 16 percent of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan appropriate for the NPP, subject to any other applicable reductions, for a service considered medically necessary.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The following policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) guidelines. A provider must make all reasonable efforts to determine whether there is other coverage for an automobile or workplace injury, such as under automobile or workers’ compensation insurance, and must promptly report as described below, in claims submitted to Humana, and any such other coverage that is identified. Additionally, a provider must bill a patient’s automobile or workplace injury insurance plan, if applicable, before billing the patient’s Humana MA plan. Finally, a provider must promptly forward to Humana any determination by an automobile or workplace insurance plan made with respect to a claim for a Humana MA enrollee’s injuries. A provider’s failure to promptly fulfill any requirement could affect Humana’s disposition of a claim after initial receipt and/or after initial adjudication. Humana expects providers to abide by the MSP billing requirements when submitting claims to Humana MA plans. If a provider identifies automobile insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter “yes” in box 10-B • Enter the accident date in field 14 • Enter all diagnosis codes in section 21 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the explanation of benefits (EOB) from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Personal injury protection (PIP) worksheet, if available – Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter occurrence code 01 or 02, as applicable, and the accident date in fields 33 – 35 • Enter value code 14 in fields 39 – 41 • Enter all diagnosis codes in fields 67 – 76 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable If a provider identifies workers’ compensation insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter “yes” in box 10-B • Enter the accident date in field 14 • Enter all diagnosis codes in section 21 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers’ compensation coverage For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter occurrence code 04 and accident date in fields 33 – 35 • Enter condition code 02, 05, or 77, as applicable, in fields 18 – 28 • Enter value code 15 or 41, as applicable, in fields 39 – 41 • Enter all diagnosis codes in fields 67 – 76 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers’ compensation coverage Note: Medicare benefits are secondary regardless of whether the patient wishes to file a workers’ compensation claim. Humana may deny a claim for healthcare services provided due to an automobile or workplace injury if it is submitted without the information above. Humana may deny a claim when payment has been made, or when payment may reasonably be expected to be made, under any applicable liability insurance arrangement, including self-insurance, no-fault insurance or workers’ compensation law or plan. Humana may also require providers to pursue and exhaust available no-fault insurance or workers’ compensation coverage and to demonstrate reasonable efforts to exhaust any other applicable coverage, before submitting claims to Humana for payment. Note: For more guidance on the MSP provisions and billing requirements, see the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ MSP booklet and the MSP manual in the References section of this policy.

policy_title: Chronic Care Management and Principal Care Management

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for principal care management (PCM), chronic care management (CCM) and complex CCM services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans may reimburse a PCM charge, CCM charge, or complex CCM charge when all of the applicable Medicare Program requirements are met. Humana requires a provider to follow all PCM and CCM requirements as outlined in the Federal Register and relevant CMS

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined below. Member Pre-Condition For PCM services, the member must be diagnosed with one chronic condition that places the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline or that is expected to last at least 3 months or until the death of the patient. For CCM services, the member must be diagnosed with at least two chronic conditions that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline and that are expected to last at least 12 months or until the death of the patient. Staff Requirement PCM and CCM services must be performed by clinical staff meeting the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1). Billing Limitations A provider may not simultaneously bill for PCM services and certain other services, including CCM, for the same member. A provider may not bill for PCM services during the surgical global period of a service for which they are reimbursed for the same member. Only one provider may bill for CCM services for a specific member per month. CCM services for a specific member must be billed for either CCM or complex CCM, but not both, per month. A provider may not bill for CCM services rendered to a member during an inpatient facility stay that is coverable by the member’s MA plan.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Humana adjudicates a claim for services provided to a plan member based on the information submitted in that claim and information related to that claim. If a qualified healthcare provider disagrees with Humana’s adjudication of that claim, based on the information submitted in that claim, that provider may submit to Humana a request for a dispute review of the plan’s determination. If a provider submits a request for a dispute review timely and with all required information, Humana will review the claim to determine whether to revise the adjudication. Humana plans may use medical records and other available relevant documentation to review a dispute . This policy establishes the applicable timeframe for a qualified healthcare provider submission of a dispute request. Note : A corrected claim is a provider’s submission of information that constitutes a material change to an existing claim. A claim submission that constitutes a material change to an existing claim is not a disagreement about Humana’s adjudication of the claim as based on the information in the previous claim submission. Therefore, Humana plans will not review a corrected claim as a dispute .

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. A qualified healthcare provider may contest the payment, denial or nonpayment of a claim in writing with at least the following information: • Member name and identification number • Date of service • Relationship of the subscriber to the patient • Claim number • Name, National Provider Identifier (NPI) and tax identification number of the provider of the services • Charge amount • Payment amount • Proposed correct payment amount • Difference between the amount paid and the proposed correct payment amount • Brief explanation of the basis for the contestation request • Relevant supporting documentation, such as, medical records, invoice, or referral form Note: Information about the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) administrative appeal processes is available at Humana.com/Appeals .

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Specific Requirements
extracted_content.content: Unless otherwise stated in the contract, an in-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 18 months from the receipt of the original claim determination. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 180 days from the receipt of the original claim determination. Multiple provider dispute requests per provider encounter are generally unacceptable. It is necessary, therefore, in a provider dispute request after an initial dispute determination, to explicitly identify specific new material information that justifies further review.

extracted_content.title: Medicaid Specific Requirements
extracted_content.content: Unless otherwise stated in the contract, an in-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 18 months from the receipt of the original claim determination. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider does not have a contractual relationship with a particular plan that would afford that qualified healthcare provider direct rights against that plan. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider lacks, for example, the right to submit a claim, the right to require the plan to process a claim seeking a member’s plan or policy benefits, the right to submit a dispute request and the right to submit corrected claims . Those examples are not exhaustive. Without waiving any provisions that prohibit an out-of-network qualified healthcare provider from assuming an enrollee’s direct rights against the plan, a plan will allow an out-of-network qualified healthcare provider to submit a dispute request within: • The timeframe established by state or federal laws, or • 180 days from the receipt of the original claim determination when the applicable state and federal laws are silent.

If a modifier is submitted, the claim is subject to review to ensure the procedure code and modifier combination is correct and the modifier was necessary. extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes Humana's expectations regarding cost-sharing for cost-share protected members.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Some members are cost-share protected under federal law, meaning that providers must not collect from those members the calculated cost-sharing for covered services. Though the collection of cost-sharing from a member might be forbidden, if there is a payer subsequent to Humana, it might be possible to collect that cost-sharing from that subsequent payer. Humana uses remittance advice remark codes (RARCs) to indicate that members are cost-share protected. For example, a specific RARC's definition might be, "Alert: Patient is a Medicaid/ Qualified Medicare Beneficiary . Review your records for any wrongfully collected deductible. This amount may be billed to a subsequent payer." A provider should note when a Humana electronic remittance advice (ERA) includes such a RARC and react to it appropriately.

extracted_content.title: Definitions of Italicized Terms
extracted_content.content: • Cost-share : Any portion of the amount allowed for a covered service that is attributed to deductible, copayment or coinsurance. • Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA) : An explanation from a health plan, such as Humana, to a provider about a claim payment. • Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) : A low-income Medicare beneficiary who receives Medicare coverage of Part A and Part B premiums and cost- sharing. • Remittance Advice Remark Codes (RARCs) : Additional explanation for an adjustment already described by a Claim Adjustment Reason Code (CARC) or to convey information about remittance processing.

This policy applies to DME and HME, collectively referred to as DME, as defined by the Indiana Health Coverage Programs. Except where noted below, providers must report DME items consistent with applicable Indiana Family and Social Services Administration (FSSA) guidance for the Indiana Health Coverage Programs.

extracted_content.content: When billing for supplies related to negative pressure wound therapy, providers must report modifier A1 – A9 with the DME item’s Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code to indicate the number of wounds for which the supply is being used. Humana uses the modifier reported when determining the number of supplies allowed per wound, as established by Indiana FSSA guidance.

extracted_content.title: Replacement
extracted_content.content: Humana may reimburse for the replacement of a medically necessary DME item that is no longer functional after the standard reasonable useful lifetime (RUL) of five years. Humana allows replacement of certain DME items using an RUL of less than five years. Humana may reimburse for the replacement before the expiration of the RUL under the following circumstances: • Irreparable damage or wear, • A change in the member’s condition that requires a change in equipment, or • Loss of the item from theft, fire or natural disaster For only the first charge for the replacement DME item, modifier RA must be billed with the DME item’s HCPCS code for one of the scenarios described above.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for durable medical equipment (DME). • • •

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

extracted_content.title: General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.content: Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans generally allow DME according to the applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. Except where guidance in this policy differs from Original Medicare, providers should follow the applicable CMS guidance. For a DME item that can be rented or purchased, whether that item is rented or purchased is subject to any applicable referral or prior authorization determination. For a DME item that can be rented, when the Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) Fee Schedule has no rental rate for that item, Humana will apply a contracted rental rate, where applicable. If there is no contracted rental rate, Humana may allow the item at the purchase rate. For a DME item that can be purchased, the amount allowed is affected by which purchase modifier is reported. • If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier NU , the amount allowed is the new equipment purchase rate. • If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier UE , the amount allowed is the used equipment purchase rate. The amount allowed for purchased used equipment is a reduced rate, typically 75%, of the new equipment purchase rate. Reimbursement for the DME item includes reimbursement for delivery and set-up. Humana does not reimburse separately for delivery and set-up. Reimbursement for covered services provided to an MA member is subject to the same special pricing rules that would apply for covered services provided to Original Medicare enrollees. For example, if a covered service provided to an Original Medicare enrollee would be priced using the Competitive Bidding Program rate, then that service provided to a Humana MA member in the same competitive bidding area is reimbursed using the same rate.

extracted_content.title: Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Capped Rental DME Items
extracted_content.subsection: Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Capped Rental DME Items
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Capped Rental DME Items
extracted_content.content: Humana requires an appropriate capped rental modifier and transaction modifier . Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as a capped rental DME item as described below. Rental If a charge for a covered capped rental DME item is submitted with modifier RR , the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate, as described below. Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. Reimbursement to a provider whose contract is not based on the Medicare DMEPOS Fee Schedule is allowed at the contracted rental rate. Otherwise, Humana allows an item, other than a power wheelchair, at a monthly rental rate of 10% of the item’s purchase rate for each of the first three months and then 7.5% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. For a power wheelchair, Humana allows at a monthly rental rate of 15% of the item’s purchase rate for the first three months and then 6% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. In both scenarios, the monthly rental rate is based on the purchase rate in effect for the date of service billed. A capped rental DME item is considered purchased after 13 continuous months of covered rental. Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR . In such cases, the amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy. Purchase Humana generally allows a purchase option for an item that CMS defines as a complex, rehabilitative power wheelchair and for certain accessories, as defined by CMS, provided for use with that wheelchair. To indicate that a charge is for the purchase of a capped rental DME item, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier . The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy.

However, Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR . Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. The two-month rental trial period does not count towards the 13-month rental period. After the two-month rental trial period, the TENS unit is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed, for one or multiple charges, reaches the applicable purchase amount or exceeds the 13-month rental period. Purchase If the TENS unit is approved for on-going use, and the unit is purchased, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier . The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy, for the month billed. If the item was previously rented, then the purchase rate is based on the purchase rate in effect at the time of the first month’s rental. The two-month rental trial period does not count towards the purchase amount. After the two-month rental trial period, the TENS unit is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed, for one or multiple charges, reaches the applicable purchase amount or exceeds the 13-month rental period.

extracted_content.content: Although transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulator (TENS) units qualify as items of IRP DME, reimbursement for TENS units differs. See the Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator section of this policy. Humana requires an appropriate transaction modifier . Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as IRP DME as described below. Rental If a charge for a covered IRP DME item is submitted with modifier RR , the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. However, Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR . An IRP DME item is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed equals the applicable purchase amount for that item. Purchase To indicate that a charge is for the purchase of an IRP DME item, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier . The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy, for the month billed. If the item was previously rented, then the purchase rate is based on the purchase rate in effect at the time of the first month’s rental, less the total amount allowed for all previous rentals.

extracted_content.title: Repair and Replacement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Repair and Replacement
extracted_content.content: Humana may reimburse the replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory after the expiration of the RUL if it is still medically necessary but no longer functional. The RUL period begins the first date of service when the specific base item, part or accessory was individually reimbursed. Additionally, the following criteria must be met: • The maximum number of allowed units has not been exceeded. • The cost to replace a part or accessory, including labor and parts, does not exceed the cost of renting or purchasing a new base item. • Base item, part or accessory replacement is not due to intentional damage, neglect or misuse of equipment. • Replacement of a part or accessory is only allowed for a member if the same member owns the base item. • The base item, part or accessory must not be under warranty. Documentation of an expired or denied warranty is required, upon request. • The base item, part or accessory is not currently being rented. Replacement Prior to the Expiration of the RUL In addition to the relevant requirements outlined above, the following conditions apply to replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL. Modifier RA Humana may reimburse the replacement of a base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL only if either of the following scenarios are true: • The member’s medical needs have changed such that a different item is medically necessary; or • The item was lost, stolen or unintentionally damaged beyond repair. For only the first charge for the replacement item, modifier RA must be billed with the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code for a base item, part or accessory replaced for one of the scenarios described above. Modifier RB Humana may reimburse the replacement of a part or accessory in association with the covered repair of a base item before the expiration of the RUL of the part or accessory when the following criteria are met: • The part or accessory is not an upgrade to the base item. • Replacement is necessary to make the base item functional. • The part or accessory is not billed on the same date of service as the base item. • The base item is not categorized as Frequently Serviced or Oxygen Equipment. • A charge for the base item was not previously denied. • The base item was previously purchased, including an item for which payment has capped through rental payments. • Modifier RR is not also billed. • Box 19 on the claim form or its electronic equivalent includes the base item code and purchase date. Modifier RB must be billed with the HCPCS code for that replaced part or accessory. When all requirements are met, the replacement of a part or accessory will be allowed at the purchase rate.

policy_title: Dental Services Inextricably Linked to Medical Services

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Dental services are generally not covered by the Medicare Program’s basic benefits. However, one exception for this coverage exclusion is for dental services that are inextricably linked to the clinical success of a covered medical service. In such cases, there must also be exchange of information, or integration, between the medical professional and the dentist. This policy establishes Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for dental services that are inextricably linked to the clinical success of a covered medical service.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s reimbursement of professional claims for services identified with “NA” in either the facility NA indicator field or the non-facility NA indicator field of the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File . According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), an “NA” in the facility NA indicator field of the MPFS Relative Value File signifies that the service is “rarely or never performed in the facility setting.” Similarly, an “NA” in the non-facility NA indicator field of the MPFS Relative Value File signifies that the service is “rarely or never performed in the non-facility setting.”

extracted_content.title: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to only professional services. Humana uses the place of service (POS) code reported on a professional claim to determine reimbursement of a service identified with “NA” in either the facility NA indicator field or the non-facility NA indicator field of the MPFS Relative Value File .

extracted_content.title: Facility POS Code
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy > Facility POS Code
extracted_content.content: For a professional claim reported with a facility POS code , Humana does not allow reimbursement for the service code and modifier combinations that CMS has identified with “NA” in the facility NA indicator field of the MPFS Relative Value File .

extracted_content.title: Non-Facility POS Code
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy > Non-Facility POS Code
extracted_content.content: For a professional claim reported with a non-facility POS code , Humana does not allow reimbursement for the service code and modifier combinations that CMS has identified with “NA” in the non-facility NA indicator field of the MPFS Relative Value File . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, claims are subject to the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky out-of-network payment policy. For more information, see the relevant guidance in the References section of this policy.

policy_title: Gender-Specific Services for Transgender or Intersex Members

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing guidance for reporting a gender-specific service for a transgender or intersex member.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage and Commercial Payment Policy
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Commercial Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Commercial Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. For a service that is not otherwise excluded, Humana allows a medically necessary gender-specific service provided to a transgender or intersex member. Humana recognizes condition code 45 and modifier KX , when submitted on a claim for a charge for a gender- specific service, as an indication that the service may be medically necessary, despite an apparent conflict between reported gender and the gender-specific service. Humana encourages providers to follow the appropriate Medicare Program guidance for correctly coding a gender-specific service and diagnosis for a transgender or intersex member. For a facility claim , Humana encourages a provider to report condition code 45 when billing for an inpatient or outpatient service that is gender-specific. For a professional claim , Humana encourages a provider to include modifier KX with a procedure code for a gender-specific service.

extracted_content.content: • Condition code 45: Gender incongruence. • Facility claim: Charges for facility services submitted on the UB-04 form, or its electronic equivalent. • Intersex: Umbrella term for people with congenital inconsistency between external genitalia, internal gonadal tissue or chromosomal sex. • Modifier KX: Requirements specified in the medical policy have been met. • Professional claim: Charges for professional services submitted on the CMS-1500 form, or its electronic equivalent; or charges for professional services submitted on the UB-04 form, or its electronic equivalent. • Transgender: Umbrella term for people whose gender identity and/or gender expression differs from what is typically associated with the sex they were assigned at birth.

extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for home health notice of admission (NOA) submissions.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. For home health agency claims: • Humana does not require an NOA for home health services. • Humana does not apply a reduction or penalty for a home health agency’s failure to submit an NOA . • Humana denies an NOA as informational when received. • Humana applies consolidated billing for home health services. Humana does not reimburse separately for services that are part of home health packaged reimbursement, even when those services are billed separately. • Humana requires a provider to report a final claim with an accurate Health Insurance Prospective Payment System (HIPPS) code, as determined by the Outcome and Assessment Information Set (OASIS), for each home health case.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Subject to all applicable limitations, such as provider contract terms, a covered item may be eligible for specific reimbursement as an implantable device only when the item is of a type that is implanted, such as a piece of tissue, a tooth, a pellet of medicine, a tube or needle containing a radioactive substance, a graft, or an insert. Also included are liquid and solid plastic materials used to augment tissues or to fill in areas traumatically or surgically removed, stents, artificial joints, shunts, pins, plates, screws, and anchors. Humana may review documentation, including but not limited to, itemized bills, invoices, and medical records, to determine whether items reported with implant revenue codes meet Humana’s definition of an implantable device. Humana requires providers to make such documentation available to Humana upon request. Humana does not reimburse an implant revenue code if the item does not satisfy Humana’s definition of an implantable device.

policy_title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination and Annual Wellness Visit

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, an initial preventive physical examination (IPPE), also known as the "Welcome to Medicare" preventive visit, is a one-time introductory visit provided during the first 12 months a Medicare beneficiary has Part B benefits. The visit may include, but is not limited to, the following: • A review of a beneficiary's medical and health-related social history. • Education and counseling about preventive services, including certain screenings, shots and referrals for other care, if needed. • Other services, such as a written plan letting the beneficiary know what preventive services the beneficiary needs. If a beneficiary has had Part B benefits for longer than 12 months, the beneficiary can receive an annual wellness visit (AWV) to develop or update a personalized prevention plan to prevent disease and disability based on the beneficiary’s current health and risk factors. The following policy outlines Humana’s reimbursement for claims for an IPPE and AWV.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage plans reimburse a charge for: • An IPPE service, HCPCS code G0402 , once per lifetime and only if provided within the first 12 months after the effective date of the member’s first Medicare Part B coverage period. • An initial AWV service, HCPCS code G0438 , once per lifetime beginning in the calendar year following the IPPE. However, the initial AWV is not dependent on reimbursement of an earlier IPPE. • A subsequent AWV service, HCPCS code G0439 , once per calendar year beginning in the calendar year following an allowed charge for HCPCS code G0438 . However, a subsequent AWV is not dependent on reimbursement of an earlier AWV or IPPE. Humana limits reimbursement of HCPCS codes G0402, G0438 and G0439 to only one of these services per calendar year.

extracted_content.subsection: Claims for Inpatient Services When an Inpatient Admission Was Not Medically Necessary
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Claims for Inpatient Services When an Inpatient Admission Was Not Medically Necessary
extracted_content.content: Humana’s Medicare Advantage plans follow the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines for inpatient Part B re- billing. When an acute care hospital determines before discharge that the patient should not have been admitted as an inpatient, Humana will only accept services submitted on an appropriate outpatient TOB 13x or 85x claim ; and will allow the provider to submit all codes that, for a normal outpatient situation, could be appropriate for that TOB; and requires condition code 44 . An inpatient claim should not be submitted. When an acute care hospital or Humana determines after discharge that the patient should not have been admitted as an inpatient, Humana will only accept services submitted on an inpatient Part B TOB 12x claim. The billing should reflect the reasonable and necessary Part B services and provide the correct Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes when available. Report condition code W2 to indicate that this is a Part B claim and include “A/B Rebilling” in the treatment authorization field. For preadmission services in the 3-day payment window , a hospital may separately bill for services provided prior to an inpatient admission and should report “A/B Rebilling” in the treatment authorization field of the appropriate outpatient TOB 13x or 85x claim . Note : When a facility fails to obtain a required inpatient authorization or the authorization request is denied, the facility must bill emergency-related services provided before the inpatient admission separately from the inpatient services. For an inpatient admission that requires authorization, Humana will deny an inpatient claim that includes unauthorized inpatient services, including charges for preadmission emergency-related services. When billed on inpatient Part B claims or outpatient claims, some services may require specific authorization.

policy_title: Itemized Bill Review for Inpatient Routine Services

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Facility billing guidelines for the UB-04 claim form, also known as the CMS-1450, and the 837 institutional electronic equivalent require providers to bill revenue codes to describe services rendered. Revenue codes are categorical and do not describe exact items, supplies and services provided during an inpatient admission. Humana may request an itemized bill for an inpatient facility claim to verify that billed revenue codes represent charges for appropriately billed items, supplies and services. Routine items, supplies and services already included in the primary inpatient room and board charge are not separately billable. Medicare Advantage Payment Policy Medicare Advantage Payment Policy In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana sometimes reviews an itemized bill for an inpatient admission to determine whether supplies, items and services specified on the itemized bill are separately billable. To separately bill for items, supplies and services rendered during an inpatient hospital encounter, the provider must consistently follow its customary charging practices for all Medicare and non-Medicare patients, for all payers and health plans. The following supplies, items and services are typically not separately billable and, therefore, not separately payable from the general room and board charge or primary service charge. Please note that the examples given do not represent an exhaustive list. • Any supplies, items and services that, under customary charging practices , are included in charges for a specific service or in charges for the delivery of services in a specific location. Examples of included supplies and items are bandages and inpatient admission kits. Examples of included services are IV flushing, dressing changes, equipment monitoring and routine nursing care and assessments. • All items and supplies that may be purchased over the counter, such as personal care items, ice packs, alcohol wipes and cotton balls. • All reusable items, supplies and equipment that are provided to all patients on a routine basis during an inpatient admission; this applies to all types of inpatient admissions, including an admission to a specific treatment area, such as a NICU or CCU, and applies to the admission of a patient who is receiving the same types of service as a patient in a specific treatment area. Examples of reusable items, supplies and equipment are cardiac monitors and durable medical equipment (DME) items used while inpatient.

The room and board charge includes the room, dietary and nursing services, minor medical and surgical supplies, medical social services, psychiatric social services and the use of certain equipment and facilities for which a separate charge is not payable. • Routine : Inpatient routine services in an inpatient facility generally are those services included by the provider in a daily service charge, sometimes referred to as the room and board charge. Some examples of routine services include the room, dietary and nursing services, minor medical and surgical supplies, medical social services, psychiatric social services and the use of certain equipment and facilities for which a separate charge is generally not payable.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Bacterial culture testing (CPT code 87081, CPT code 87070, CPT code 87071) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in cases of viral pharyngitis. • Amplification testing (CPT code 87651) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in cases of viral pharyngitis. • Rapid antigen diagnostic testing (RADT) (CPT code 87880) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE for any of the following: – As a follow-up test to bacterial culture test (CPT code 87081, CPT code 87070, CPT code 87071) for a Streptococcal infection within the prior 14 days – In cases of viral pharyngitis • Serological titer testing (CPT code 86060, CPT code 86215) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in patients with Streptococcus . • Direct probe testing (CPT code 87650) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE if amplification testing (CPT code 87651) for Streptococcus has been performed on the same date of service. • The following tests ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE in patients with Streptococcus or Enterococcus : – Anti-streptolysin O immunoassay (CPT code 86060, CPT code 86063) – Tests that screen and identify multiple Streptococcal strains, using either immunoassay or nucleic acid-based assays, such as the Solana Strep Complete Assay and the Lyra Direct Strep Assay (CPT code 83789, CPT code 87430) • The quantification of any strain of Streptococcus using nucleic acid amplification, including polymerase chain reaction (PCR), (CPT code 87652) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

policy_title: Laboratory – Biochemical Markers of Alzheimer’s Disease and Dementia

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • For individuals with a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, measurement of the following biomarkers IS REIMBURSABLE: – Amyloid beta peptides (CPT Code 82233, CPT code 82234, CPT code 0358U) – The ratio (CPT code 0459U) of total tau (t-tau) (CPT code 84394) to amyloid beta 1-42 (Aβ42) (CPT code 82234) – The ratio (CPT code 0445U) of phosphorylated tau 181 (p-tau181) (CPT code 84393) to Aβ42 (CPT code 82234) – The ratio of p-tau 217 (p-tau217) (CPT code 84393, CPT code 0479U) to Aβ42 (CPT code 82234) • When not ordered in conjunction with Aβ42 (CPT code 82234), measurement of the following biomarkers IS NOT REIMBURSABLE: – t-tau (CPT code 84394) – p-tau181 (CPT code 84393) – p-tau217 (CPT code 84393, CPT code 0479U) • For individuals with a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, measurement of other biomarkers (CPT code 83520, CPT code 83884, CPT code 0547U) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • For individuals with a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, measurement of all other cerebral spinal fluid biomarkers (CPT code 0393U, CPT code 0443U, CPT code 0548U) or plasma biomarkers (CPT code 0479U, CPT code 0551U) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • The use of DISCERN™ (CPT code 0206U*, CPT code 0207U*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • The use of other multianalyte assays (CPT code 0412U*, CPT code 0503U*, CPT code 0568U*, CPT code 0596U) for Alzheimer’s disease or dementia IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • Gene expression profiling to predict development of Alzheimer’s disease (CPT code 0289U**) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. policy_title: Laboratory – Biomarkers for Myocardial Infarction and Chronic Heart Failure

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Quantitative measurement of cardiac troponin T or I (CPT code 84484) for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction (MI) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals presenting with any of the following: – Ischemic chest pain – Pain in the upper abdomen, shoulders, upper arms, forearms, wrists, fingers, neck and throat, lower jaw and teeth or back pain – Shortness of breath, belching, nausea, indigestion, vomiting, diaphoresis, dizziness, lightheadedness, clamminess or fatigue – Squeezing, tightness, pressure, constriction, crushing, strangling, burning, heartburn, fullness in the chest, band-like sensation, knot in the center of the chest, lump in throat, ache, heavy weight on chest or toothache when there is radiation to the lower jaw • A maximum of four serial quantitative troponin tests (CPT code 84484) IS REIMBURSABLE in the first three days after presentation. • Testing for natriuretic peptide, such as B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) or N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT- proBNP) (CPT code 83880*) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals presenting with dyspnea or shortness of breath. • Testing for BNP or NT-proBNP (CPT code 83880*) IS REIMBURSABLE every rolling 12 months for individuals presenting with any of the following: – Acute or chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure – Chronic heart failure: systolic, diastolic or combined systolic and diastolic – Chronic right heart failure • Measurement of the following cardiac biomarkers for the diagnosis or prognosis of MI IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in conjunction with the measurement of cardiac troponin T or I: Policy Number : LAB2023001 – Cardiac creatine kinase isoenzyme myocardial band (CK-MB) (CPT code 82553, CPT code 82554) – Copeptin (CPT code 84588) – C-reactive protein (CPT code 86140) – Creatine kinase (CK) (CPT code 82550) – CK isoenzymes (CPT code 82552) – Heart-type fatty acid binding protein (H-FABP) (CPT code 82725) – Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (CPT code 83625) – Myoglobin (CPT code 83874) • For individuals with signs and symptoms of acute coronary syndrome, quantitative measurement of cardiac troponin T or I (CPT code 84484) by an independent laboratory IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • In the outpatient setting, qualitative measurement of cardiac troponin T or I (CPT code 84512) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • In the outpatient setting, testing of growth stimulation expressed gene 2 (ST2) or its isoforms (CPT code 83006) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of apolipoprotein B (Apo B) (CPT code 82172**) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following: – Diabetes mellitus – Disorder of galactose, lipoprotein, or amino acid transport metabolism – History of circulatory system disorders – Hypertriglyceridemia – Obesity or metabolic syndrome – Presence of coronary angioplasty implant • Once per lifetime measurement of lipoprotein (a) [Lp(a)] (CPT code 83695**) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals 18 years of age or older. • Measurement of homocysteine (CPT code 83090****) or conventional measurement of C-reactive protein (CPT code 86140) as a part of a risk assessment for cardiovascular disease (CVD) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Measurement of novel lipid and non-lipid biomarkers (CPT code 82610*, CPT code 83700**, CPT code 83701**, CPT code 83704**, CPT code 83719**, CPT code 83880***, CPT code 85384, CPT code 85415) as a part of a risk assessment for CVD IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Direct measurement of small dense low-density lipoprotein (LDL) (CPT code 83722) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE except in diagnoses of Cushings syndrome, chronic kidney disease (CKD), obstruction of the bile duct or pregnancy. • CVD risk panels consisting of multiple individual biomarkers intended to assess CVD (CPT code 0052U, CPT code 0308U**, CPT code 0309U**, CPT code 0415U**, CPT code 0541U**) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE. • Measurement of lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 (Lp-PLA2) (CPT code 83698****) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • All other biomarker panels designed to detect CVD risk (CPT code 0019M**, CPT code 0377U) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE. • Measurement of components of a lipid panel (CPT code 82465*****, CPT code 83718*****, and CPT code 84478*****) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE on the same date of service as a lipid panel (CPT code 80061*****).

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • For individuals with a diagnosis of either type 1 or type 2 diabetes, measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE once every three months. • For individuals with a diagnosis of prediabetes, annual screening for type 2 diabetes with a measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE. • Screening for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes with a measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE once every 3 years in individuals 18 years of age and older with any of the following: – Cardiovascular disease – Family history of diabetes – High-risk race/ethnicity (e.g., African American, Latino or Hispanic, Native American, Asian American or Pacific Islander) at risk for type 2 diabetes (e.g., obesity) – History of gestational diabetes – Hypercholesterolemia – Hypertension – Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) – Metabolic syndrome – Other clinical conditions associated with insulin resistance (e.g., acanthosis nigricans) – Overweight or obese – Physical inactivity – Polycystic ovary syndrome • Screening for diabetes with an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) (CPT code 82951, CPT code 82952) or measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE once every 3 years for children ages 10 – 17 with at least one of the following: – Acanthosis nigricans – Dyslipidemia – Family history of type 2 diabetes – Hypertension – Overweight or obese – Polycystic ovary syndrome • For individuals 10 years of age or older who have been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF), screening for CF-related diabetes with an OGTT (CPT code 82951, CPT code 82952) IS REIMBURSABLE once every 365 days. • For pregnant individuals, an OGTT (CPT code 82951, CPT code 82952) IS REIMBURSABLE up to once per month during pregnancy.

extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • At a general wellness exam, testing for chlorinated pesticides (CPT code 82441), including dichlorodiphenyldichloroethylene (DDE) and dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT), using a blood, serum, plasma, saliva, urine or stool sample IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • At a general wellness exam for individuals over the age of four, testing blood, serum, plasma, saliva, urine or stool sample IS NOT REIMBURSABLE for any of the following: – 5-Hydroxyindolacetic acid (5-HIAA) (CPT code 83497) – Amino acids (CPT code 82127, CPT code 82136, CPT code 82139) – Allergen-specific immunoglobulin G (IgG) (CPT code 86001*) – Behenic acid (CPT code 82542) – Carotene or beta-carotene (CPT code 82380) – Carnitine (CPT code 82379^^) – Citrate (CPT code 82507) – Elastase (CPT code 82653, CPT code 82656) – Fat differentiation, qualitative or quantitative (CPT code 82705, CPT code 82710, CPT code 82715) – Fat stain (CPT code 89125) – Gastrointestinal fat absorption study (CPT code S3708) – Glutathione (CPT code 82978) – Homovanillic acid (HVA) (CPT code 83150) – Lignoceric acid (CPT code 82542) – Lipid peroxides (CPT code 82542) – Prealbumin (CPT code 84134) – Vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) (CPT code 84585) • At a general wellness exam, testing blood, serum, urine, cerebrospinal fluid, fingernails, hair or stool sample IS NOT REIMBURSABLE for any of the following: – Cadmium (CPT code 82300***) – Chromium (CPT code 82495***) – Copper (CPT code 82525***) – Heavy metal, qualitative or quantitative (CPT code 83015***, CPT code 83018***) – Magnesium (CPT code 83735*^) – Manganese (CPT code 83785***) – Nickel (CPT code 83885***) – Organic acids, qualitative or quantitative (CPT code 83918, CPT code 83919, CPT code 83921) – Selenium (CPT code 84255***) – Tocopherol alpha, also known as vitamin E (CPT code 84446^^) – Vitamin A (CPT code 84590^^) – Volatiles (CPT code 84600) – Zinc (CPT code 84630***)

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • The following tests ARE REIMBURSABLE for any of these conditions: bleeding, inflammation, itching, pain, pelvic infection, pregnancy with history of pre-term labor, redness and vaginitis: – Aptima® BV Assay (CPT code 81513**) – BD MAX™ Vaginal Panel (CPT code 81514**) – Direct probe deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) based identification of Gardnerella (CPT code 87510*), Trichomonas (CPT code 87660*) and Candida (CPT code 87480*) – Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) based identification of Gardnerella vaginalis (CPT code 87511*, CPT code 87512*) – NAAT or PCR based identification (CPT code 87661*) of Trichomonas vaginalis – PCR based identification of Candida (CPT code 87481*, CPT code 87482*) – Testing for the presence of amines (CPT code 82120) – Xpert® Xpress Mutliplex Vaginal Panel (MVP) (CPT code 81515***) • Screening for Trichomonas (CPT code 87660*, CPT code 87661*) IS REIMBURSABLE for any of the following risk factors: – Exchange of sex for payment – History of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) – Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) – Incarceration – Injection drug use – New or multiple partners • For asymptomatic individuals, including asymptomatic pregnant individuals at an average or high risk for premature labor, screening for trichomoniasis or bacterial vaginosis (CPT code 87480*, CPT code 87510*, CPT code 87661*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Rapid identification of Trichomonas by enzyme immunoassay (CPT code 87808) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans

extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services.
