extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE for individuals with a diagnosis of either Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes once every three months. • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE once every 365 days to help in the detection and diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes in individuals aged 18 and over with any of the following: – Overweight or obese – Pre-diabetes – History of gestational diabetes – Family history of diabetes – Cardiovascular disease – Hypertension – Hypercholesterolemia – Metabolic syndrome – Polycystic ovary syndrome – High-risk race/ethnicity (e.g., African American, Latino or Hispanics, Native American, Asian American, Pacific Islanders) at risk for Type 2 diabetes (e.g., obesity) – Physical inactivity – Other clinical conditions associated with insulin resistance (e.g., acanthosis nigricans) • Diabetes screening with a hemoglobin A1c determination (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE once every 3 years for children aged 10-17 with at least one of the following characteristics: – Overweight or obese – Family history of type 2 diabetes – Hypertension – Dyslipidemia – Polycystic ovary syndrome • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE for pregnant individuals up to once per month during pregnancy. • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE when billed in conjunction with measurement of (CPT code 82985) fructosamine.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • For individuals with a confirmed diagnosis of hepatitis B virus (HBV), testing for Immunoglobulin M antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (IgM anti-HBc) (CPT code 86705) or for HBV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) (CPT code 87516, CPT code 87517) IS REIMBURSABLE . • Antibody testing for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection (CPT code 86803, CPT code 86804) IS REIMBURSABLE in any of the following situations : – For screening in pregnant individuals – Once per lifetime for all individuals over 18 years of age – One test every 90 days for any individual with recognized conditions or exposures in any of the following situations: ▪ Children born from an HCV-positive individual ▪ Current sexual partners of HCV-infected persons ▪ Evidence of liver disease ▪ History of incarceration ▪ History of or current hemodialysis ▪ Illicit drug use ▪ Illicit intranasal ▪ Injectable drug use ▪ Presence of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection ▪ Receipt of a blood transfusion or blood component ▪ Receipt of a tattoo ▪ Receipt of an organ transplant • Testing for HCV genotype (CPT code 87902) IS REIMBURSABLE with a confirmed diagnosis of HCV. • Qualitative nucleic acid testing for HCV ribonucleic acid (CPT code 87520, CPT code 87521) IS REIMBURSABLE: – With a confirmed diagnosis of HCV: up to 12 tests per year – As a one-time screen for perinatally exposed infants who are less than one year of age • Quantitative nucleic acid testing for HCV viral load (CPT code 87522) IS REIMBURSABLE once per month not to exceed seven tests in 18 months. • For individuals who have tested negative for HBV and HCV, antibody testing for hepatitis A virus (HAV) (CPT code 86708, CPT code 86709) IS REIMBURSABLE. • For individuals who have tested positive for HBV, antibody testing for hepatitis D virus (HDV) (CPT code 86692, CPT code 87380) IS REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of serum free testosterone based on total serum testosterone (CPT code 84403**), sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG) (CPT code 84270) or bioavailable testosterone (CPT code 84410*) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following conditions: – Acromegaly – Acute and chronic kidney failure – Benign prostatic hypertrophy – Cirrhosis or hepatitis – Diabetes mellitus – Erectile dysfunction – Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease – Hyperthyroidism – Hypothyroidism – Infertility – Nephrotic syndrome – Obesity – Polymorphisms – Use of estrogens – Use of glucocorticoids, progestins or androgenic steroids • Testing for serum total testosterone measurements (CPT code 84403**) IS REIMBURSABLE at the designated frequency in any of the following situations: – For individuals taking enzyme inhibitors for prostate cancer: as needed – For individuals receiving testosterone replacement therapy: up to eight tests every four years – Gender-dysphoric or gender-incongruent persons: as needed – Infertility: as needed – Symptomatic individuals being evaluated for polycystic ovary syndrome or functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: as needed • Measurement of serum dihydrotestosterone (CPT code 82642) IS REIMBURSABLE for diagnosing 5-alpha reductase deficiency in individuals with ambiguous genitalia, hypospadias or microphallus. • Measurement of serum estradiol (CPT code 82670, CPT code 82681) IS REIMBURSABLE for the following conditions at the designated frequency: – For individuals with gynecomastia: once per lifetime – For individuals who are experiencing infertility: as needed • Testing for serum total testosterone (CPT code 84403**), free testosterone (CPT code 84402) or bioavailable testosterone (CPT code 84410*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in asymptomatic individuals or in individuals with non-specific symptoms.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of either serum lipase (CPT code 83690) or amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration for the initial diagnosis of acute pancreatitis IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals presenting with any of the following signs and symptoms: – Abdominal distention – Abdominal pain – Abnormal weight loss – Acute pancreatitis – Anorexia – Cullen sign – Diarrhea – Fever – Grey Turner sign – Hypoactive bowel sounds – Hypotension – Hypoxemia – Ileus – Nausea or vomiting – Tachycardia – Tachypnea • Measurement of either serum lipase (CPT code 83690) or amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration IS NOT REIMBURSABLE more than once per week. • Measurement of serum amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration IS NOT REIMBURSABLE when billed in conjunction with serum lipase concentration (CPT code 83690). • Measurement of either serum lipase (CPT code 83690) or amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in any of the following situations: – For all other situations or conditions not described above – For asymptomatic individuals during a general exam without abnormal findings – For individuals with a diagnosis of chronic pancreatitis • Measurement of serum or urine trypsin, trypsinogen or trypsinogen activation peptide (TAP) (CPT code 83519) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in any of the following situations: – For asymptomatic individuals during a general exam without abnormal findings – For individuals with a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis • Measurement of the following biomarkers with a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis IS NOT REIMBURSABLE : – C-reactive protein (CRP) (CPT code 86140, CPT code 86141) – Interleukin-6 (IL-6) (CPT code 83529) – Interleukin-8 (IL-8) (CPT code 83520) – Procalcitonin (CPT code 84145) Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans

In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Serum intact parathyroid (PTH) testing (CPT code 83970*) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following conditions at the designated frequency: - As needed for individuals who have: ▪ The following signs of hypoparathyroidism: - Abnormal magnesium - Elevated serum phosphorus - Hypercalciuria - Hypocalcemia - Low calcitriol ▪ Abnormal calcium ▪ Familial medullary thyroid carcinoma ▪ Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A ▪ Osteoporosis or low bone mass ▪ Undergone parathyroidectomy - One test per year for individuals who have been diagnosed with hyperparathyroidism but who have not undergone parathyroidectomy - One test every 12 months for individuals who have been diagnosed with stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) - One test every three months for individuals who have been diagnosed with stage 4 or stage 5 CKD - One test every three months for individuals who are younger than 18 years of age and who have been diagnosed with pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A or type 1B, pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism, progressive osseous heteroplasia or acrodysostosis - One test per year for individuals who are 18 years of age or older and who have been diagnosed with pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A or type 1B, pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism, progressive osseous heteroplasia or acrodysostosis Policy Number : LAB2023049 • The following tests ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE for individuals with a primary diagnosis representing a general encounter without abnormal findings: - Serum, blood or fecal magnesium testing (CPT code 83735**) - Serum ionized calcium (CPT code 82330) or urine calcium testing (CPT code 82340) - Urine phosphorus or phosphate testing (CPT code 84105) Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans

policy_title: Laboratory – Testing for Crohn’s Disease, Ulcerative Colitis and Irritable Bowel Syndrome

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Fecal calprotectin testing (CPT code 83993) IS REIMBURSABLE when any one of the following conditions or symptoms are present: – Abdominal or pelvic pain – Abnormal weight loss – Anal spasm or anal fistula – Anemia – Constipation – Crohn’s disease – Diarrhea – Duodenitis – Dysphagia – Early satiety – Fecal incontinence – Flatulence – Functional dyspepsia – Gastro-esophageal reflux disease – Heartburn – Hemorrhage of anus or rectum – Irritable bowel syndrome – Malnutrition or malabsorption – Melena – Nausea and vomiting – Other specified diseases of the intestine, anus or rectum – Oral aphthae – Noninfective gastroenteritis and colitis – Symptoms and signs involving the digestive system – Ulcerative colitis – Use of steroids, immunosuppressants or immunomodulators • Fecal lactoferrin measurement (CPT code 83630, CPT code 83631) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • The use of the following serologic markers ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE in individuals with Crohn’s Disease, ulcerative colitis or irritable bowel syndrome: – Antibody to Escherichia coli outer membrane porin C (anti-OmpC) (CPT code 83520) – Antibody to Pseudomonas fluorescens-associated sequence I2 (anti-I2) (CPT code 83520) – Anti-CBir1 flagellin antibody (anti-cBir1) (CPT code 83520) – Antichitobioside antibodies (ACCA IgA) (CPT code 83516) – Anti-cytolethal distending toxin B (anti-CdtB) and anti-vinculin antibodies (CPT code 0176U) – Antilaminaribioside antibodies (ALCA IgG) (CPT code 83516) – Antimannobioside antibodies (AMCA IgG) (CPT code 83516) – Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) (CPT code 86036, CPT code 86037) – Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibody (ASCA) (CPT code 86671) – Perinuclear anti-neutrophilic cytoplasmic antibody (pANCA) (CPT code 86021, CPT code 86255) – Pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) (CPT code 83520) • The use of diagnostic algorithm-based testing (CPT code 0164U) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Genetic testing for inflammatory bowel disease, including Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, (CPT code 0203U*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Immunoglobulin G (IgG) based food sensitivity testing (e.g., inFoods® IBS Test) (CPT code 0598U) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

policy_title: Laboratory – Testing for Diagnosis of Active or Latent Tuberculosis

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • An interferon gamma release assay (IGRA) (CPT code 86480, CPT code 86481) and an acid fast bacilli (AFB) smear or stain (CPT code 87116) ARE REIMBURSABLE to diagnose latent tuberculosis (TB) infection for individuals at risk for infection based on clinical presentation or risk factors noted below upon screening evaluation: ▪ Abnormal weight loss ▪ Acute kidney failure or chronic renal disease ▪ Cough ▪ Crohn's disease ▪ Diabetes mellitus ▪ Enlarged lymph nodes ▪ Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease ▪ Immunodeficiency ▪ Lymphoma, leukemia or multiple myeloma ▪ Malignant neoplasm of head, face and neck ▪ Nonspecific reaction to cell mediated immunity measurement of gamma interferon antigen response ▪ Nonspecific reaction to tuberculin skin test without active tuberculosis ▪ Opioid or illicit substance use ▪ Pericardial effusion ▪ Pleural effusion ▪ Pulmonary nodule ▪ Rheumatoid arthritis ▪ Steroid or immunosuppressant use ▪ Transplanted organ and tissue status when screening is mandated • For individuals diagnosed with TB, nucleic acid testing for Mycobacterium (CPT code 87551, CPT code 87556, CPT code 87561) IS REIMBURSABLE. • For individuals with active tuberculosis, IGRA (CPT code 86480, CPT code 86481) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Quantitative nucleic acid testing for Mycobacterium species (CPT code 87552), M. tuberculosis (CPT code 87557) and M. avium complex (CPT code 87562) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Genotyping of Mycobacterium species (CPT code 87150, CPT code 87153) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Adenosine deaminase (ADA) (CPT code 84311) levels in cerebrospinal, pleural, peritoneal, pericardial and other fluids for the diagnosis of extrapulmonary TB IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Tests designed to detect or diagnose TB through detection of serum biomarkers (CPT code 0574U) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: Babesiosis
extracted_content.content: 1. To detect Babesia microti , Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests ( NAAT) testing, including Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) testing, (CPT code 87469) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with one of the following symptoms: • Body aches • Chills • Fatigue • Fever • Hemolytic anemia • Hepatomegaly • Insect bite • Jaundice • Splenomegaly • Weakness

extracted_content.title: Babesiosis
extracted_content.content: 2. For individuals with a diagnosis of Babesiosis, the use of either an Immunoglobulin G (IgG) or Immunoglobulin M (IgM) indirect immunofluorescence antibody (IFA) assay (CPT code 86753) for Babesia IS NOT REIMBURSABLE .

extracted_content.title: Borrelia
extracted_content.content: 1. To detect Borrelia spp., NAAT testing, including PCR testing, (CPT code 87478), an IFA assay for Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies (CPT code 86619) or detection by immunoblot of Immunoglobulin G (IgG) or Immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody (CPT code 0043U, CPT code 0044U) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with one of the following symptoms: • Arthralgia • Chills • Headache • Insect bite • Myalgia • Nausea • Vomiting

extracted_content.title: Dengue Virus
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Dengue Virus
extracted_content.content: 1. For individuals with a diagnosis of classical or hemorrhagic dengue fever, the hemagglutination inhibition test (CPT code 86280) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: Ehrlichiosis and Anaplasmosis
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Ehrlichiosis and Anaplasmosis
extracted_content.content: 1. To detect Anaplamsa phagocytophilum or Ehrlichia chaffeensis, NAAT testing, including PCR testing, of whole blood (CPT code 87468, CPT code 87484) or an IFA assay for Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies (CPT code 86666) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with one of the following symptoms: • Fever • Gastrointestinal issues, including nausea, vomiting and diarrhea • Headache • Insect bite • Malaise • Myalgia • Shaking chills

extracted_content.title: Plasmodium (Malaria)
extracted_content.content: 1. The use of an IFA assay for Plasmodium antibodies (CPT code 86750) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: Rickettsiosis
extracted_content.content: 1. The use of an IFA assay for Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies to Rickettsia (CPT code 86757) IS REIMBURSABLE twice when at least two weeks has passed between tests and IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following symptoms: • Abdominal pain • Anorexia • Chills • Fever • Headache • Insect bite • Malaise • Myalgia • Nausea • Photophobia • Skin rash • Ulcerative lesion with regional lymphadenopathy for Rickettsia species 364D rickettsiosis • Vomiting

extracted_content.title: Rickettsiosis
extracted_content.content: 2. For individuals with a diagnosis of typhus fever or Rickettsiosis, blood culture testing (CPT code 87040) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: West Nile Virus
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > West Nile Virus
extracted_content.content: 1. The use of an IFA assay for Immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies specific to West Nile virus (CPT code 86788, CPT code 86789) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following symptoms: • Abdominal pain • Altered level of consciousness • Arthralgia • Fatigue • Fever • Headache • Insect bite • Maculopapular rash • Myalgia • Nausea • Neck stiffness • Vision loss • Vomiting • Weakness

extracted_content.title: West Nile Virus
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > West Nile Virus
extracted_content.content: 2. For individuals with a diagnosis of West Nile virus infection, the use of an IFA assay for Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies specific to West Nile virus (CPT code 86789) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

extracted_content.title: Zika Virus
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Zika Virus
extracted_content.content: 1. NAAT testing including, PCR testing, (CPT code 87662*) or Immunoglobulin M (IgM) testing (CPT code 86794*) for Zika virus IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following symptoms: • Abnormal brain development • Conjunctivitis • Decreased joint movement • Feeding problems • Fever • Headache • Hearing loss • Joint pain • Microcephaly • Muscle pain or stiffness • Rash • Seizures • Suspected exposure to Zika virus • Ultrasound findings consistent with congenital Zika virus • Vision problems

extracted_content.title: General
extracted_content.content: 1. For asymptomatic individuals, testing for Babesiosis, Borrelia, Dengue virus, Ehrlichiosis and Anaplasmosis, Plasmodium, Rickettsiosis, West Nile virus or Zika virus with the tests discussed above IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans *The payment criterion for CPT code 86794, CPT code 87662 apply to all Medicare jurisdictions, except those states awarded to Noridian Healthcare Solutions, LLC.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • A nuclear matrix protein (NMP22) test (CPT code 86386*) or a bladder tumor antigen (BTA) test (CPT code 86294*, CPT code 86316*) IS REIMBURSABLE in individuals with a bladder neoplasm or a personal history of bladder neoplasm. • For all other situations not described above, an NMP22 test or a BTA test IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Fluorescence immunocytology tests (e.g., ImmunoCyt/uCyt+) (CPT code 88346, CPT code 88350) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE as part of a screening for malignant neoplasm of the bladder or in individuals with the following symptoms: – Dysuria or painful or frequent micturition – Hematuria – Low back pain – Pyuria or other abnormal findings • Urinary protein biomarker panels designed to detect, monitor or predict recurrence of bladder cancer (e.g., Oncuria® Detect, Oncuria® Monitor, Oncuria® Predict) (CPT code 0365U***, CPT code 0366U***, CPT code 0367U***) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE . • All other urinary biomarker panels designed to diagnose or prognose bladder cancer (CPT code 0012M, CPT code 0013M, CPT code 0363U, CPT code 0420U, CPT code 0452U**, CPT code 0465U**, CPT code 0549U**, CPT code 0613U) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE .

policy_title: Long-Acting Reversible Contraception While Inpatient Postpartum

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s reimbursement for long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) provided to a postpartum inpatient. LARC devices are a type of birth control that provides long-term pregnancy prevention. They are the most effective form of reversible birth control, with a failure rate of less than one percent. There are two types of LARC devices: intrauterine devices (IUDs) and implants.

extracted_content.title: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to only facility services. As used in this policy, x represents any appropriate frequency code, which is the final digit of the type of bill (TOB) code. Humana reimburses for a LARC device inserted for a postpartum inpatient separately from the inpatient hospital labor and delivery Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) payment. In such circumstances, insertion of the LARC device is reimbursed at the fee schedule rate. To facilitate such payment, the facility should submit a UB-04 claim form or its electronic equivalent with TOB 11x. The facility should report insertion of the LARC device with HCPCS codes J7296, J7297 , J7298 , J7300 , J7301 or J7307 . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, claims are subject to the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky out-of-network payment policy. For more information, see the relevant guidance in the References section of this policy.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) allows some physicians and practitioners to opt out of the Medicare Program for a period of two years. At the end of two years, a provider can opt in to the Medicare Program, or continue to opt out for another two-year period. Providers should refer to CMS and relevant Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) publications to understand the formal opt-out process. Providers who opt out of the Medicare Program agree to the following conditions during their opt-out period: • A provider and a Medicare beneficiary, including a Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plan member, must enter into a private contract for services that the Medicare Program would otherwise cover. Limitations on charges imposed by the Medicare Program are not applicable to services furnished by opt-out providers under a private contract. Therefore, the beneficiary agrees to pay for all services furnished by the opt-out provider based on the terms of their private contract. • A provider must not request payment from the Medicare Program during the opt-out period. – Exception: Providers can request payment from the Medicare Program for emergency or urgently needed services when no private contract exists between the beneficiary and the opt-out provider. Providers are required to submit the claim to the Medicare Program on behalf of the beneficiary for emergency or urgently needed services when no private contract exists between the beneficiary and the opt-out provider. Limitations on charges imposed by the Medicare Program are applicable for emergency or urgently needed services. • A provider must not contract with a Medicare beneficiary at the time the beneficiary is seeking emergency or urgently needed services.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

extracted_content.title: Effect of Private Contract
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Effect of Private Contract
extracted_content.content: In no case do Humana MA plans reimburse a charge for a service rendered pursuant to a valid private contract between an opt-out provider and an MA member. Humana may recoup any claim payment made for a service furnished by an opt-out provider if it is determined a private contract between the opt-out provider and the MA member was in effect at the time the service was furnished.

extracted_content.title: Non-Emergency and Non-Urgent Care Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Non-Emergency and Non-Urgent Care Services
extracted_content.content: Humana MA plans deny a charge submitted by an opt-out provider for a service that is not an emergency or urgent care service.

extracted_content.title: Emergency and Urgent Care Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Emergency and Urgent Care Services
extracted_content.content: Humana MA plans may reimburse a charge for a service rendered and submitted by a provider who has opted out of the Medicare Program only for an emergency or urgent care service, and only if the provider does not have a private contract with the MA member. An opt-out provider must report modifier GJ when submitting a charge for an emergency and urgent care service. Medical records must be available to substantiate that the service was truly for an emergency or urgent care service. Humana MA plans deny a charge submitted by an opt-out provider without modifier GJ . extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's expectations for a provider charging a patient for a missed appointment.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans recognize that a provider can charge a patient for a missed appointment, as long as the provider applies their policy according to the standards outlined in Chapter 1, Section 30.3.13 of the Medicare Claims Processing Manual. Therefore, a provider must apply any policy regarding a missed appointment equally to all patients, whether they are enrolled in the Medicare Program or not. A missed appointment fee must be the same for Medicare beneficiaries and patients who are not Medicare beneficiaries. The fee is not a charge for a health care service but compensates the provider for a missed business opportunity. A hospital may charge a patient for a missed appointment in the hospital’s outpatient department only if the patient is not receiving inpatient services at the time of the missed appointment. The hospital would violate 42 CFR 489.22 if it were to charge a registered hospital inpatient a fee for missing an appointment in the hospital’s outpatient department. Consistent with Original Medicare, Humana MA plans do not reimburse for a missed appointment charge imposed by a provider. A missed appointment fee should not be billed to Humana. If a provider submits a charge to Humana for a missed appointment fee, Humana will deny the charge, indicating the service is not covered under the patient’s MA plan.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following applies to professional services only. Modifier 22 may be added to a procedure code to indicate that the work required to provide a service was substantially greater than is typically required. Documentation must support the substantial additional work and the reason for the additional work. Examples of circumstances that might require substantial additional work for which it is appropriate to report modifier 22 include increased intensity, time or technical difficulty of the service; increased severity of the patient’s condition; and increased physical or mental effort required to provide the service. Additional service time alone does not justify the use of modifier 22 . Modifier 22 should be reported only with a procedure code that has a global surgery period of 0, 10 or 90 days. Modifier 22 should not be appended to an evaluation and management (E/M) service. Humana determines additional reimbursement, if any, for a procedure code submitted with modifier 22 , based on individual consideration of unusual circumstances as documented in the medical record or operative report. Humana does not allow more than the billed charge amount for a procedure code submitted with modifier 22 .

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Bilateral procedures are procedures that are performed on similar sites on opposite sides of the body, during the same session, by the same qualified health care practitioner. When a procedure reported using a service code with a Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File (RVF) bilateral indicator 1 is performed bilaterally, providers must report the code with either modifier 50 or with anatomical modifiers such as modifiers LT and RT . Humana strongly encourages providers to report a bilateral procedure using modifier 50 rather than modifiers LT and RT , but accepts both methods. When using modifier 50 to report a bilateral procedure, report a single claim line with a unit of 1. When using modifiers LT and RT to report a bilateral procedure, report two claim lines, each with a unit of 1. Only report modifier 50 when the procedure is performed on similar but opposite sites. For example, report modifier 50 for the same service code for a procedure performed on the right and left knee. However, do not report modifier 50 for the same service code for a procedure performed on the right knee and left shoulder. When reporting two or more bilateral procedures using the same code, report the first bilateral procedure on a single claim line with a unit of 1 using modifier 50 and report a single claim line with a unit of 1 for all subsequent bilateral procedures using modifier 50 and modifier 59. It is not necessary to report modifier 50 with a service code with an MPFS RVF bilateral indicator other than 1.

extracted_content.subsection: Special considerations for billing modifier 50 with certain anatomical modifiers
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Billing > Special considerations for billing modifier 50 with certain anatomical modifiers
extracted_content.content: Report modifier 50 in addition to eyelid, finger and toe modifiers on one claim line with a unit of 1 for procedures performed bilaterally on similar but opposite sites. Examples that are considered bilateral and should be billed with the appropriate anatomical modifiers and modifier 50 : • Upper left eyelid and upper right eyelid: Report modifiers E1 and E3 with modifier 50 • Left hand, third digit and right hand, third digit: Report modifiers F2 and F7 with modifier 50 • Left foot, great toe and right foot, great toe: Report modifiers TA and T5 with modifier 50 Examples that are not considered bilateral and should be billed as two claim lines, each with a unit of 1, with the appropriate anatomical modifiers but not with modifier 50 : • Upper left eyelid and lower right eyelid: Report modifiers E1 and E4 • Left hand, third digit and right hand, fourth digit: Report modifiers F2 and F8 • Left foot, great toe and right foot, third digit: Report modifiers TA and T7

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement
extracted_content.content: Humana only applies a bilateral payment adjustment to procedures reported using a service code with a MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1. When a bilateral payment adjustment applies, the amount allowed for a bilaterally performed procedure is the lesser of the following: • The total charged for both sides; or • 150 percent of either – the provider's contracted rate that would have applied if the procedure had been done unilaterally or – the base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan , for an out-of-network provider, that would have applied if the procedure had been done unilaterally. A single claim line with an MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1 code billed with modifier 50 is processed as one unit. Providers may submit supporting documentation for reconsideration of additional units. In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when a bilaterally performed procedure is reported with another procedure for the same date of service, a multiple procedure payment reduction may be applied after the bilateral payment

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement
extracted_content.content: adjustment. In such cases, the bilaterally performed procedure is considered one unit.

extracted_content.title: Examples
extracted_content.content: Bilateral payment adjustment (BPA): Humana allows 150 percent of the base amount allowed for MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1 codes reported with a modifier 50 . Bilateral payment adjustment (BPA) and multiple surgery reduction (MSR): The multiple surgery reduction is applied after the bilateral payment adjustment. For this Medicare Advantage example, Humana plans apply a multiple surgery reduction as follows: • The procedure with the highest base amount allowed after bilateral payment adjustments is not reduced; and • All other procedures are reduced by 50 percent. Therefore, service code bbbbb is allowed at 100 percent of the base amount allowed, service code ccccc is allowed at 50 percent of 150 percent of the base amount allowed and service code ddddd is allowed at 50 percent of the base amount allowed.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: In some situations, it is necessary for two surgeons to work together, each as a primary surgeon, on the same patient during the same operative session due to factors such as the complexity of the procedure or the condition of the patient. This can include surgeries when two surgeons of different specialties are required for a specific procedure. This can also include surgeries in which two surgeons perform elements of the procedure simultaneously such as during bilateral knee replacement or a heart transplant. In such circumstances, the physicians are considered co-surgeons, not assistant surgeons. Note: Surgeons of different specialties performing distinct procedures, even if the procedures use the same incision site, are not considered co-surgeons.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier CT to report computed tomography (CT) services furnished on equipment that is not consistent with dose optimization standards established by the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA). Enforcement of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013, also known as the MITA Smart Dose standard, for the Medicare Program is required by the Protecting Access to Medicare Act of 2014. The criteria of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013 ensure use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. The standard outlines four attributes CT equipment should meet to ensure that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies. Performing CT services on equipment that meets all elements of the standard helps reduce a patient’s lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members’ exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards, including NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for services reported with modifier CT .

Humana requires providers to follow the appropriate Medicare Program guidance for correct coding using modifier CT . Providers must report modifier CT with procedure codes for applicable CT services performed on equipment that does not meet all four attributes of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. Humana reduces reimbursement for the technical component ( TC) of an applicable CT service reported with modifier CT by five percent for dates of service in 2016 and by 15 percent for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017. Note: Pre-authorization requirements may apply when applicable CT services are provided to a Humana member.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) global surgical policy states that reimbursement for a procedure that has a global surgical package includes payment for preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care, as well as payment for various related services, such as complications following surgery, postsurgical pain management and supplies. There are occasions when more than one qualified healthcare practitioner provides services included in the global surgical package of a surgery. For example, the physician who performs the surgical procedure may not provide the follow-up care. In situations in which, for a global surgical package that may be split, there is an agreed transfer of care, it is appropriate to reimburse the various practitioners for portions of the global surgical package . For a surgery with a global surgical package , a qualified healthcare practitioner indicates the portion of the global surgical package performed by using modifiers 54, 55 and 56 , as appropriate. This policy outlines Humana’s reimbursement for a service reported with modifier 54, 55 or 56 .

extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to global surgery procedure codes as identified on the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File and applies only to charges for practitioner services. Humana plans determine the amount allowed for a segment of split global care for a service with a global surgery period as outlined below. Humana allows a charge for preoperative management only, indicated by modifier 56 , at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan for the service multiplied by that service’s MPFS preoperative percentage. Humana allows a charge for intraoperative care only, indicated by modifier 54 , at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan for the service multiplied by that service’s MPFS intraoperative percentage. Humana allows a charge for postoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 55 , at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan for the service, multiplied by that service’s MPFS postoperative percentage, and multiplied by the percentage of the global surgery period for which the billing practitioner provided care. Effectively, the total of all percentages of a global surgery period for which practitioners were responsible for postoperative management is 100%. Therefore, the plan does not allow more than 100% of the postoperative management for that service. Humana expects a practitioner to report, in the units field on the claim form, the number of days of service that the practitioner provided, consistent with the transfer of postoperative management to which the practitioners agreed. However, if a Medicare A/B MAC directs providers to report the number of days differently, Humana MA plans permit out-of-network providers in the jurisdiction to report days consistent with the MAC 's guidance. Humana considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for both preoperative management and intraoperative care , unless there is a coverable charge for the same procedure code for preoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 56 . If there is a coverable charge submitted with modifier 56 for the same service, the plan considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for intraoperative care only.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana expects each healthcare provider to administer drugs and biologicals, collectively referred to as drugs, efficiently and in a clinically appropriate manner. This includes using multi-dose vials or packages when available and clinically appropriate. Humana also expects providers to use the combination of available single-dose vials or packages that results in the least amount of discarded drug. For example, if: • A drug is only available in single-dose 500 milligram and 120 milligram vials, • 540 milligrams are administered, and • The Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code defines one base unit of the code as 10 milligrams, Then five of the 120 milligram vials should be used, resulting in a discarded amount of 60 milligrams (6 units). It is not appropriate to use a combination of one 500 milligram vial and one 120 milligram vial, resulting in a discarded amount of 80 milligrams (8 units). Humana reimburses for the discarded amount of a drug when all of the following criteria are satisfied: • The drug is a covered expense, • The discarded amount is the remainder of a single-dose vial or package used to treat the patient, and • The drug is billed as described below. When those criteria are satisfied, Humana reimburses no more, for the total administered and total discarded, for a drug than the amount appropriate, in dollars, for the efficient administration amount of the drug.

extracted_content.title: Billing For a Discarded Amount
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Commercial Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Commercial Payment Policy > Billing For a Discarded Amount
extracted_content.content: When there is a discarded amount of drug from a single-dose vial or package, Humana expects providers to report modifier JW according to applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. When, as discussed above, a discarded amount is reimbursable for a date of service, the billing provider must submit two lines, as described below, using the HCPCS code appropriate for that drug for that date of service: The number of base units submitted for each of the two lines must be calculated using the appropriate unit size indicated by the HCPCS code description. The first of the two lines must indicate the number of base units appropriate for the amount administered to the patient, with fractions rounded up to the next highest whole number of base units . For example, if: • 14 milligrams are administered and • The HCPCS code defines one base unit of the code as 10 milligrams, Then the first of the two lines must indicate 2 units of the HCPCS code because the 14 milligrams administered are one base unit of the HCPCS code and a fraction of a second base unit of the HCPCS code. The second of the two lines, with modifier JW appended, must indicate the number of base units that is the difference between the efficient administration amount and the number of base units indicated on the first of the two lines. Continuing the example above, if: • 14 milligrams are administered, • The HCPCS code defines one base unit of the code as 10 milligrams, and • Of the vials available for provider purchase, the amount that results in the least amount of discarded drug is one 30 milligram vial Then the second of the two lines must indicate 1 unit of the HCPCS code because • The efficient administration amount is 30 milligrams, • The number of base units for the efficient administration amount is 3, and • The difference between the number of base units for the efficient administration amount (3) and the number of base units indicated on the first of the two lines (2) is 1. For each of those two lines, the provider must submit a charge amount that is the charge amount applicable per base unit multiplied by the number of base units indicated for that line. Continuing the example above: For each drug with a reimbursable discarded amount for a date of service, the combined amount charged for both lines must not exceed the total charge that would be appropriate if, for the efficient administration amount , the provider had administered all of each vial or package used. If the number of base units that would be appropriate for the billing of the first of two lines equals the number of base units for the efficient administration amount , then, instead of submitting two lines, the provider submits only one line with modifier JZ . For example, if: • 40 milligrams are administered, • The HCPCS code defines one base unit of the code as 25 milligrams, and • Of the vials available for provider purchase, the amount that results in the least amount of discarded drug is two 25 milligram vials, Then only one line is submitted and must indicate 2 units of the HCPCS code because the 40 milligrams administered are one base unit of the HCPCS code and a fraction of a second base unit of the HCPCS code. Suppliers who dispense but do not administer drugs from single-dose vials and packages should report modifier JW when there was a discarded amount of drug during the preparation process before supplying the drug. In addition to the limitations described above, Humana will deny a line reported with modifier JW when: • The billing provider submitted the line with a procedure code that is not a drug code, • The billing provider submitted that line to report a multi-dose vial or package, • The billing provider did not also submit a line for the administered amount, without modifier JW , for the same drug code and date of service, or • The combined number of units submitted for both lines exceeds the total base units for the efficient administration amount .

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing expectations for reporting Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) modifiers XE , XP , XS and XU , known collectively as modifiers X{EPSU} .

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Each one of the modifiers X{EPSU} defines a unique subset of distinct procedural services. Modifier 59 is used to report distinct procedural services more generally without the specificity provided by modifiers X{EPSU} . Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) instructions from the American Medical Association (AMA) state that modifier 59 should not be used if a more descriptive modifier is available to report the special circumstances. When one of the modifiers X{EPSU} more accurately describes the circumstances of a distinct procedural service than modifier 59 , Humana encourages the reporting of that modifier, instead of modifier 59 . Modifiers X{EPSU} should not be appended to evaluation and management (E/M) services.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines various multiple procedure payment reductions (MPPR). Practitioner reimbursement for a procedure code generally includes reimbursement for the individual costs, also known as inputs, typically associated with that service. For example, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) uses a formula that accounts for the inputs associated with a procedure code to determine Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) reimbursement rates for that code. When the same provider renders multiple services, or multiple units of the same service, to the same patient on the same day, the total calculation for the procedure code(s) could account more than once for an input that was only rendered once. Examples of inputs that might be contemplated in reimbursement for certain procedure codes, that would not typically be duplicated in the same encounter include: greeting and gowning the patient; preparing the room, equipment and supplies; providing education and obtaining consent. An MPPR adjusts reimbursement to offset duplication of reimbursement for inputs that were only rendered once.

extracted_content.title: Diagnostic Cardiovascular Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Diagnostic Cardiovascular Services
extracted_content.content: For diagnostic cardiovascular services, the portion of an in-network practitioner’s contracted rate that is attributable to the technical component (TC) may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic cardiovascular services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a TC , all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan is attributable to the TC . For reimbursement of both a TC and a professional component (PC) , the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan that is attributable to the TC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code’s MPFS local TC amount to the code’s MPFS local global amount. For example: 𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌 𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥 𝑻𝑻𝑻𝑻 𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚 𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌𝐌 𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥𝐥 𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠𝐠 𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚𝐚 Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic cardiovascular TC services rendered by the same provider . To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge or to one or more units of a charge with multiple allowed units: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a TC , Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 6. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge’s per-unit practitioner’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan that is attributable to TC , as described above. Finally, Humana eliminates from review the unit of service that is ranked highest; or, if multiple units of service are ranked highest, Humana eliminates one of those units. Humana applies MPPR to all other allowed units of service. When Humana determines to apply diagnostic cardiovascular services TC MPPR to a unit, a 25 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit’s practitioner’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan that is attributable to TC . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply.

Diagnostic Imaging Professional Component For diagnostic imaging services, the portion of an in-network practitioner’s contracted rate that is attributable to the PC may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic imaging services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan that is attributable to the PC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a PC , all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan is attributable to the PC . To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge or to one or more units of a charge with multiple allowed units: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a PC , Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 4. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge’s per-unit practitioner’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan that is attributable to PC , as described above. extracted_content.title: Multiple Endoscopic Procedures
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Multiple Endoscopic Procedures
extracted_content.content: For endoscopic services rendered by an in-network practitioner, the contracted rate may be subject to MPPR. For endoscopic services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan may be subject to MPPR. Humana applies an MPPR to same-family endoscopic procedures, including multiple units of the same procedure code, rendered by the same provider on the same day. To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing, Humana identifies, for a date of service, all MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 3 endoscopy codes and identifies each service’s base endoscopy code. Second, Humana groups all services with the same endoscopy base code. Each group of services with the same base code is one endoscopic family. Third, when there are multiple procedure codes for an endoscopic family and one of those is the family’s base code, Humana denies separate reimbursement for that base code charge. Reimbursement for the base code is included in reimbursement for the highest ranked procedure code in that endoscopic family. Humana ranks all reimbursable services within each endoscopic family by the procedure’s contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan . Finally, within each endoscopic family, Humana reduces reimbursement for each procedure code, except that family’s highest ranked procedure. The amount Humana uses to reduce reimbursement for a procedure code is the amount allowed for the procedure’s base code. When a contracted rate does not include an amount allowed for a base code, Humana will apply the following formula based on amounts provided by CMS. These amounts are used to create a reduction amount. The reduction amount is then applied to the contracted rate. Endoscopic procedures are also subject to multiple surgery reduction. As discussed in the Multiple Surgery section below, each endoscopic family is treated as a single surgery for determination of a multiple surgery reduction. information.

extracted_content.title: Multiple Surgery
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Multiple Surgery
extracted_content.content: Humana applies a multiple surgery reduction when: • The same provider performs more than one same-day MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 2 service; or • The same provider performs endoscopic procedures in more than one endoscopic family on the same day (see Multiple Endoscopic Procedures section above); or • The same provider performs at least one MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 2 service and at least one endoscopic procedure on the same day. In unique circumstances, for the purposes of applying a multiple surgery reduction: • Humana may not consider an MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 2 service as a surgery. • Humana may consider a service that does not have an MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator of 2 as a surgery. Multiple surgery reduction applies to same-day services whether or not those services were submitted with modifier 51 , modifier 59 or modifiers X{EPSU}. Humana plans apply a multiple surgery reduction as follows: • The procedure with the highest contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan is not reduced; and • All other procedures are reduced by 50 percent. Special Rules for Endoscopic Services For an endoscopic service, multiple endoscopy reduction and multiple surgery reduction are determined separately. This will result in one of the following scenarios, depending on the number of services billed and the individual multiple procedure indicator code of each service : • Multiple endoscopy reduction alone could apply to the service. • Multiple surgery reduction alone could apply to the service. • Both multiple endoscopy reduction and multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service. • Neither multiple endoscopy reduction nor multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service. If multiple endoscopy reduction applies, it is always determined before multiple surgery reduction. After determining any multiple endoscopy reductions, all endoscopic services in the same endoscopic family are treated as a single service for the purpose of determining multiple surgery reduction, as follows: • For multiple surgery reduction ranking purposes, endoscopic procedures in the same endoscopic family are treated as one service. • An endoscopic family’s multiple surgery reduction ranking establishes the multiple surgery reduction percentage, if any, for all services in that endoscopic family. Note : Additional payment rules may apply in certain circumstances. For example, when a bilateral adjustment is applicable, it will be applied before a multiple surgery reduction.

extracted_content.title: Definitions of Italicized Terms
extracted_content.content: • Always Therapy: A service that is always considered a therapy, as noted in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File by a multiple procedure indicator 5. • Base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a unit of a covered expense, determined by the member’s plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments. • Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, multiple procedure indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for practitioner services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table. Elements of the file that are referenced in this policy include the following: – CF: The conversion factor is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year. – PE GPCI: The practice expense geographic price index for the area where the service was rendered, shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year. – PE RVU: The practice expense relative value unit is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year. • Modifier 26: Professional component. • Modifier 51: Multiple procedures. • Modifier 59: Distinct procedural service. • Modifier TC: Technical component. • Modifiers X{EPSU}: Modifiers XE, XP, XS and XU, collectively. – Modifier XE : Separate encounter. – Modifier XP : Separate practitioner. – Modifier XS : Separate structure. – Modifier XU : Unusual non-overlapping service. • Practice Expense (PE): One of three groups of inputs used to determine pricing of services covered under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS); PE accounts for costs of running a practice (other than expenses associated with professional liability and the practitioner’s actual work), including rent, equipment, supplies and staff costs other than the work performed by the practitioner personally. • Professional Component (PC): The professional component of a service is for practitioner work interpreting a diagnostic test or performing a procedure and includes indirect practice and malpractice expenses related to that work. • Same Provider: A single qualified practitioner or multiple practitioners within the same group practice. • Technical Component (TC): The technical component of a service is for all non-practitioner work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s national drug code (NDC) billing requirements.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional and facility claims, except inpatient facility claims. The NDC is the industry standard for identifying the specific drug administered. Reporting the NDC enables accurate and timely claims adjudication. Other than the exceptions outlined in this policy, Humana requires a provider to report an accurate, valid NDC with a Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) drug code. Humana denies a HCPCS drug code submitted without an NDC. A denied HCPCS drug code that requires an NDC can be resubmitted with an NDC, within timely filing guidelines, for reconsideration of

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: payment. To eliminate the need to try to determine whether an NDC would be required in a specific scenario, Humana strongly encourages providers to submit each HCPCS drug code with the accurate, valid corresponding NDC. Exceptions An NDC is not required with the following: • Child and adult immunization drug codes; • Gene therapy drug codes; • Hemophilia drug codes; and • Radiopharmaceutical drug codes.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Reporting an NDC
extracted_content.content: Humana requires the following when reporting an NDC: • For CMS-1500 paper claims: Report the NDC qualifier N4 followed by the 11-digit NDC in box 24. • For UB-04 paper claims: Report the NDC qualifier N4 followed by the 11-digit NDC in box 43. • For electronic claims: Report the NDC in loop 2410. Report NDC qualifier N4 in segment LIN 02 and the NDC in segment LIN 03. • When using different vial sizes that share the same HCPCS drug code but have different NDCs, for the same patient, bill multiple lines in order to report each unique NDC. • Report the NDC in a 5-4-2 digit format. If necessary, add a zero, as indicated in the examples below. • Do not report dashes, as indicated in the examples below.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) provides continuous care to a critically ill neonate and involves many advanced technologies and interventions that are unique to the specialty area. These critically ill neonates can suffer from various medical conditions including congenital heart defects, neural tube defects, prematurity, respiratory distress, metabolic disorders and difficulties with feeding and growth. Diagnosis related groups (DRGs), including Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Groups (MS-DRGs) and All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Groups (APR-DRGs), are assigned to newborns based on factors including, but not limited to, birth weight, extent of prematurity, diagnoses, severity of illness, and associated significant problems. NICU is comprised of four levels of care: Level 1, Level 2, Level 3 and Level 4. Each of the four levels of care has a corresponding revenue code: 0171, 0172, 0173 and 0174, respectively. This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for NICU claims. Please note the definitions and background information for the following terms that are relevant for this policy: • Neonate: An infant who is less than four weeks old. • Prematurity: The condition when a neonate is born before a gestational age of 37 weeks and zero days. • Extreme prematurity: The condition when a neonate is born before a gestational age of 28 weeks and zero days. • Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.0): Occurs when there is a deficiency of

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: surfactant. This is primarily due to insufficient production of surfactant or in rare cases, it can be caused by a genetic mutation in surfactant proteins or the transporter genes. Prematurity is the primary cause as surfactant production by the lungs does not occur until around a gestational age of 26 weeks, so the majority of cases are seen in the extreme premature

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: population. In total, all case-types of newborn respiratory distress occurs in approximately 7 percent of deliveries with only about 1 percent resulting in RDS. Prematurity and low birth weight are the most important risk factors in the development of RDS and usually occurs before a gestational age of 28 weeks. Chest X-ray findings for RDS are classic. The findings include diffuse atelectasis, with a ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms and low lung volumes. Treatment includes surfactant therapy; assisted ventilation with a ventilator, continuous positive airway pressure (regular or nasal), or other assisted ventilation such as high flow oxygen; monitoring of oxygenation; and supportive care (thermoregulation, nutritional support, fluid and electrolyte management, etc.) • Transient tachypnea of the newborn (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.1): A transient respiratory distress caused when fetal lung fluid that is not readily absorbed from the lungs during the delivery process. Chest X-ray findings show lungs that are normal or hyperinflated. There is noted perihilar streaking, and the lung fissures can demonstrate fluid in them. Treatment is oxygen and supportive care. This typically resolves within a few days. • Other respiratory distress of newborn (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.8): Respiratory distress that occurs in the neonatal period that is related to a specific disease process. Examples include respiratory distress secondary to pneumonia, sepsis, meconium aspiration, congenital heart defect, etc. • Respiratory distress of newborn, unspecified (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.9): Respiratory distress that occurs in the neonatal period that is not related to a specific identified disease process or does not meet the definition of transient tachypnea of the newborn or RDS. extracted_content.title: Florida Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. To be reimbursed for a medically necessary NICU stay subject to DRG-based pricing, the provider must satisfy the requirements in this policy. During the NICU stay, the provider must provide all relevant documentation, such as medical records, for utilization management and leveling purposes. Humana uses all relevant documentation to assign the DRG for the case according to the table below. For a case that qualifies for more than one DRG, Humana assigns the DRG associated with the most complex services. Humana uses all relevant documentation to review the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes reported on the claim according to the peer- reviewed literature definition and treatment requirements. If a reported diagnosis code does not satisfy the applicable requirement, it is not considered when calculating the DRG reimbursed. Humana reviews the level of care as reported by the NICU revenue code according to the table below. If the documentation associated with a charge for a NICU revenue code does not establish that the criteria associated with that revenue code were satisfied, reimbursement for the claim will instead be calculated using the highest NICU revenue code for which the criteria are satisfied.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. To be reimbursed for a medically necessary NICU stay subject to DRG-based pricing, the provider must satisfy the requirements in this policy. During the NICU stay, the provider must provide all relevant documentation, such as medical records, for utilization management and leveling purposes. Humana uses all relevant documentation to assign the DRG for the case according to the table below. For a case that qualifies for more than one DRG as outlined in the table below, Humana assigns the DRG associated with the most complex services. Humana uses all relevant documentation to review the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes reported on the claim according to the peer- reviewed literature definition and treatment requirements. If a reported diagnosis code does not satisfy the applicable requirement, it is not considered when calculating the DRG reimbursed. For a claim with a discharge date on or after May 29, 2025, Humana reviews additional factors to calculate reimbursement of the DRG outlier payment, when applicable, according to CMS MS-DRG guidelines. This includes reviewing whether the provider has billed for any days that do not meet medical necessity requirements. It also includes reviewing the following data on the claim: • The level of care as reported by the NICU revenue code, according to the applicable criteria established by MCG Health; • The number of days billed; and • The dates of service.

extracted_content.title: Oklahoma Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. To be reimbursed for a medically necessary NICU stay subject to DRG-based pricing, the provider must satisfy the requirements in this policy. Providers must follow all applicable Oklahoma Health Care Authority (OHCA) guidance for NICU claims outlined at OHCA’s Payment for Newborns website, available in the References section, including but not limited to the following: • Report the ICD-10-CM diagnosis code indicating the neonate’s birth weight. During the NICU stay, the provider must provide all relevant documentation, such as medical records, for utilization management and leveling purposes. Humana uses all relevant documentation to assign the DRG for the case according to the tables below. For a case that qualifies for more than one DRG, Humana assigns the DRG associated with the most complex services. Humana assigns the MS-DRG according to the table below. Humana uses all relevant documentation to review the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes reported on the claim according to the peer- reviewed literature definition and treatment requirements. If a reported diagnosis code does not satisfy the applicable requirement, it is not considered when calculating the DRG reimbursed. Humana reviews the level of care as reported by the NICU revenue code according to the table below. If the documentation associated with a charge for a NICU revenue code does not establish that the criteria associated with that revenue code were satisfied, reimbursement for the claim will instead be calculated using the highest NICU revenue code for which the criteria are satisfied.

extracted_content.title: Virginia Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: To be reimbursed for a medically necessary NICU stay subject to DRG-based pricing, the provider must satisfy the requirements in this policy. During the NICU stay, the provider must provide all relevant documentation, such as medical records, for utilization management and leveling purposes. Humana uses all relevant documentation to assign the DRG for the case according to the table below. For a case that qualifies for more than one DRG, Humana assigns the DRG associated with the most complex services. Humana uses all relevant documentation to review the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes reported on the claim according to the peer- reviewed literature definition and treatment requirements. If a reported diagnosis code does not satisfy the applicable requirement, it is not considered when calculating the DRG reimbursed. Humana reviews the level of care as reported by the NICU revenue code according to the table below. If the documentation associated with a charge for a NICU revenue code does not establish that the criteria associated with that revenue code were satisfied, reimbursement for the claim will instead be calculated using the highest NICU revenue code for which the criteria are satisfied.
