extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Observation services are specific, clinically appropriate, outpatient services provided to help a healthcare professional decide whether a patient needs to be admitted as an inpatient or can be discharged. This policy outlines the criteria that Humana plans use to determine appropriate billing and documentation of facility observation services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to facility services only. For Humana Medicaid plans, this policy applies except when not permissible by state Medicaid guidelines.

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: The billing of facility observation services is appropriate only when the observation services were medically necessary, the observation services were ordered by a qualified healthcare professional , the patient was under the care of a physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner during observation services, and one or more of the following is true of the encounter: • Treatment and monitoring were provided to determine if inpatient admission was needed • The observation services were provided for patient monitoring, after outpatient surgery or diagnostic testing, that was beyond the standard recovery period for the service • A qualified healthcare professional directly referred the patient to the facility for observation services • The patient was a child who was observed because of an uncertain clinical response to outpatient therapy • The patient was a child whose parent or caregiver was unavailable or unknown If none of those events occurred, a Humana plan does not reimburse for a facility observation charge. The billing of and reimbursement for observation services are limited to rendered observation services that were specifically medically necessary and typically do not exceed 48 hours. Any time for any of the following scenarios is excluded from the calculation of billable observation hours: • Patient monitoring during diagnostic or therapeutic services, including observation care interrupted by such services • Routine preparation for outpatient surgery and diagnostic testing • Services provided during the standard recovery period after outpatient surgery, which is four to six hours, or after diagnostic testing • Services provided for the convenience of the patient, physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner • Observation services provided according to a standing order • The time period between the order for observation services and when observation services began • The time period between observation services ending and the patient’s discharge • The time period between observation services ending and the arrival of the patient’s transportation

extracted_content.title: Documentation of Observation Services
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Documentation of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Humana reserves the right to request medical records, at any time, to confirm accurate billing of observation services. Medical record documentation for observation services must include: • The physician’s or qualified nonphysician practitioner’s assessment that determined the patient would benefit from observation services • The order for observation services • The start and stop times of observation services • Time for non-observation services that interrupted observation care, if any • Nurses’ notes • Progress notes on the patient’s condition and treatment to confirm the continuing need for observation services • Supporting diagnostic and ancillary test reports, if any • Discharge notes including the discharge order

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Section 1833(q) of the Social Security Act requires charges for some Medicare Program services to be submitted with ordering or referring provider information from a qualified healthcare provider . This requirement ensures quality of care because many services require a qualified healthcare provider to interpret and provide guidance to the patient. Supplying a valid National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the ordering or referring qualified healthcare provider helps in the verification that services rendered were necessary and medically reviewed and that follow-up care is available. Original Medicare began rejecting claims without valid ordering or referring provider information January 6, 2014.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

extracted_content.title: Valid Order or Referral Requirement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Valid Order or Referral Requirement
extracted_content.content: Humana plans require valid orders for the same types of services for which Original Medicare requires orders and require valid referrals for the same types of services for which Original Medicare requires referrals . To be valid, an order or referral must have been issued by a qualified healthcare provider . The services of a Part A home health agency, specifically, may only be ordered or referred by a doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy or doctor of podiatry. Humana plans deny charges for services for which Humana requires valid orders or referrals when those services were provided in the absence of an applicable, valid order or referral ; when appropriate, plans require reimbursement of overpayments .

extracted_content.title: Order or Referral Documentation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Order or Referral Documentation
extracted_content.content: Humana requires providers to maintain complete and accurate documentation of orders and referrals for services for which Humana requires orders and referrals . Humana requires providers to make order and referral documentation available to Humana upon

extracted_content.title: Order or Referral Documentation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Order or Referral Documentation
extracted_content.content: request. Humana plans deny charges for services that lack appropriate order or referral documentation; when appropriate, plans require reimbursement of overpayments .

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Claim Submission

extracted_content.content: Facility billing guidelines for the UB-04 claim form, also known as the CMS-1450, and the 837 institutional electronic equivalent require providers to bill revenue codes to describe services furnished. Revenue codes are categorical and do not provide detailed descriptions of specific items, supplies and services provided during an outpatient encounter. Medicare Advantage Payment Policy Medicare Advantage Payment Policy In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to outpatient facilities that include, but are not limited to, hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgery centers. To separately bill for items, supplies and services, a provider must consistently follow its customary charging practices for all Medicare and non-Medicare patients, for all payers and health plans. Humana sometimes reviews an itemized bill for an outpatient encounter to determine whether supplies, items and services specified on the itemized bill are separately billable. The following supplies, items and services are typically not separately billable and, therefore, not separately payable from primary service charge(s). Please note that the examples given do not represent an exhaustive list. • Any supplies, items and services that, under customary charging practices , are included in charges for a specific service or in charges for the delivery of services in a specific location. Examples of included supplies and services are bandages, IV flushing, dressing changes, equipment monitoring and routine nursing care and assessments. • All items and supplies that may be purchased over the counter, such as personal care items, ice packs, alcohol wipes and cotton balls. • All reusable items, supplies and equipment that are provided to all patients on a routine basis during an outpatient encounter; this applies to all outpatient encounters. Examples of reusable items, supplies and equipment are cardiac monitors and durable medical equipment (DME) items used while in an outpatient facility.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Pass-through billing occurs when a provider bills for a service for which neither that provider nor any individual under that provider’s direct employment performed that service. One common example is that a provider ordered a service and bills for it, but an unaffiliated lab performed the service. Sub-contracted individuals are not under “direct employment.”

extracted_content.title: Purpose
extracted_content.content: To facilitate compliance with Humana’s state and federal obligations to ensure fair and accurate payment of health care claims for covered services, to avoid duplicate payments, overpayments and subsequent recoupments, to prevent fraud, waste and abuse, and to ensure accurate member copay, deductible and coinsurance obligations for members under their health benefit plan in compliance with all state and federal laws, rules and regulations.

extracted_content.title: Scope
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all services to the extent that its application is not prohibited by applicable contract provisions and applicable state or federal law, rules and regulations including Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) instructions.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

extracted_content.title: General
extracted_content.content: Pass-through billing is generally prohibited, with limited exceptions, for Medicare Advantage basic benefits (i.e., benefits that would be covered under Original Medicare Parts A and B). A provider may not bill, charge, seek payment or have any recourse against Humana or any Humana Medicare Advantage member for any amounts related to a denied pass-through billed service for basic benefits.

extracted_content.title: Limited Exceptions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Limited Exceptions
extracted_content.content: The following are limited exceptions to the general prohibition against pass-through billing. A provider may submit a charge for potentially covered services rendered by another qualified provider under only the following circumstances. In all of these circumstances, the submitting provider may not bill an amount greater than the amount the submitting provider paid or will pay the rendering provider for the service. Humana will not pay any amount greater than the amount the submitting provider pays the rendering provider for the service. The billing provider must make available to Humana documentation of the amount paid to the rendering provider.

extracted_content.title: Laboratories billing for referred tests exception
extracted_content.subsection: Laboratories billing for referred tests exception
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Limited Exceptions > Laboratories billing for referred tests exception
extracted_content.content: A referring laboratory may bill for clinical laboratory diagnostic tests performed by a reference laboratory if one of the following conditions is met: • The referring laboratory is located in, or is part of, a rural hospital; or • The referring laboratory is wholly owned by the entity performing such tests, the referring laboratory wholly owns the entity performing such tests, or both the referring laboratory and the entity performing such tests are wholly-owned by a third entity; or • The referring laboratory does not refer more than 30 percent of the clinical laboratory tests for which it receives requests during the year, not counting referrals made under the wholly-owned condition described above.

extracted_content.title: Purchased diagnostic or screening tests exception
extracted_content.subsection: Purchased diagnostic or screening tests exception
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Limited Exceptions > Purchased diagnostic or screening tests exception
extracted_content.content: Note: This section does not apply to clinical diagnostic laboratory tests paid by Original Medicare under the Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule. A physician or other professional may bill for the technical component (TC) and/or professional component (PC) of a diagnostic test that was ordered by the physician or other professional, or ordered by a party related to the billing physician or other supplier through common ownership or control. However, anti-markup payment limitations apply if the diagnostic test is performed by a physician who does not “share a practice” with the billing physician or other professional. The performing provider for the TC is the professional who conducted or supervised the test, and the performing provider for the PC is the professional who interpreted the results. Under anti-markup payment limitations, payment to the billing physician or other professional, minus beneficiary cost-sharing, for the TC or PC of the diagnostic test may not exceed the lowest of the following amounts: • The performing provider’s net charge, excluding any charges for equipment or space leased, to the billing physician or other professional; • The billing physician’s or other professional’s actual charge; and • The amount for the test that would be allowed if the performing provider billed directly.

extracted_content.title: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.subsection: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Limited Exceptions > Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.content: If the performing physician is deemed to “share a practice” with the billing physician or other professional who ordered the test, the anti-markup payment limitation does not apply. A performing physician is considered to “share a practice” with the billing physician or other professional if either: • The performing physician provides “substantially all” (at least 75 percent) of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional, as discussed below; or • The services were performed under a “site of service/same building” arrangement as discussed below. The “substantially all” services requirement will be satisfied if, at the time the billing physician or other professional submits a claim for a service provided by the performing physician, the billing physician or other professional has a reasonable belief that: • For the 12 months prior to and including the month in which the service was performed, the performing physician provided substantially all of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional; or • The performing physician will provide substantially all of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional for the next 12 months (including the month in which the service is performed). The performing physician may be deemed to “share a practice” with the billing physician or other professional if the services were performed under a “site of service/same building” arrangement. This alternative approach requires the performing physician to be an owner, employer or independent contractor of the billing physician or other professional and requires that the TC or PC be performed in the “office of the billing physician or other supplier.” The “office of the billing physician or other supplier” is any medical office space, regardless of the number of locations, in which the ordering physician or other professional regularly provides patient care. It also includes space where the billing physician or other supplier furnishes diagnostic testing services, if the space is located in the “same building” in which the ordering physician or other ordering professional regularly provides patient care. With respect to a billing physician or other professional that is a “physician organization,” the “office of the billing physician or other supplier” is space in which the ordering physician provides substantially the full range of patient care services the ordering physician provides generally. “Same building” and “physician organization” are defined in 42 CFR §411.351. The billing physician or other professional must keep on file the performing physician’s name, address and the National Provider Identifier. The physician or other professional providing the TC or PC of the diagnostic test must be enrolled in the Medicare Program. No formal reassignment is necessary.

extracted_content.content: A charge submitted by a Social Security Act Section 1861(u) "provider of services," for a service rendered by another provider that, under Original Medicare, would be payable to the Section 1861(u) "provider of services." A “provider of services” includes a hospital, critical access hospital, skilled nursing facility, comprehensive outpatient rehabilitation facility, home health agency, hospice program or, for certain purposes, a fund.

extracted_content.content: Any other exceptions applicable to the Original Medicare Program.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: There are some codes on the Kentucky Department for Medicaid Services (DMS) Physician Administered Drug (PAD) List that do not have rates in the Kentucky Medicaid fee schedule. This policy outlines how Humana establishes rates for those codes.

extracted_content.title: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional services only. As outlined in Kentucky DMS guidance, for all drug and biological codes, Humana requires a provider to submit a charge with the valid, corresponding National Drug Code (NDC). When a reimbursement rate for a code on the PAD List is not listed on the Kentucky Medicaid fee schedule, Humana allows the following reimbursement for that PAD : • For a charge reported with place of service (POS) code 11 : Medicare’s average sales price (ASP) plus 6% • For a charge reported with POS code 12 : Manufacturer’s average wholesale price (AWP) minus 15% • For a charge reported with POS code 22 : Manufacturer’s AWP minus 15% Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, claims are subject to the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky out-of-network payment policy. For more information, see the relevant guidance in the References section of this policy.

extracted_content.title: Definitions of Italicized Terms
extracted_content.content: • Physician Administered Drug (PAD) : Physician Administered Drugs are drugs other than vaccines that are covered under section 1927(k)(2) of the Social Security Act and are typically administered by a medical professional in a physician’s office or other outpatient clinical setting. • Place of service (POS) code 11 : Office – Location, other than a hospital, skilled nursing facility (SNF), military treatment facility, community health center, State or local public health clinic, or intermediate care facility (ICF), where the health professional routinely provides health examinations, diagnosis, and treatment of illness or injury on an ambulatory basis. • Place of service (POS) code 12 : Home – Location, other than a hospital or other facility, where the patient receives care in a private residence. • Place of service (POS) code 22 : On Campus-Outpatient Hospital – A portion of a hospital’s main campus which provides diagnostic, therapeutic (both surgical and nonsurgical), and rehabilitation services to sick or injured persons who do not require hospitalization or institutionalization. (Description change effective January 1, 2016)

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s preventable inpatient readmission review standards.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to facility services only. For Humana Medicaid plans, this policy applies except when not permissible by state Medicaid guidelines.

extracted_content.title: General Readmission Review Requirements
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > General Readmission Review Requirements
extracted_content.content: All readmissions, to the same facility , reimbursed using Diagnosis Related Group (DRG ) methodology are subject to review to determine if the readmission was preventable.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: If Humana determines that a readmission was preventable, Humana does not allow payment for the second admission since reimbursement for the first admission includes reimbursement for the second admission. The following are examples of preventable readmissions. This is not an all-inclusive list: • Premature discharge that resulted in a readmission. This is based on information that the provider or physician knew, or should have known, at the time of discharge. • Care rendered during the second admission that should have occurred during the first admission. • An inappropriate transfer. • A readmission that was not medically necessary. • A readmission that is an attempt to circumvent Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) payment.

extracted_content.title: Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.content: If Humana determines that a subsequent admission was not preventable or was unrelated to the prior admission, Humana may allow separate payment for each admission. The following are examples of admissions that may be separately payable: • An admission that is due to a reoccurrence of a chronic condition and is not a continuation of the previous episode’s admission. • An unrelated readmission, including an unrelated same-day readmission. Facilities cannot be held responsible for readmissions beyond their control, which may include, but are not limited to, the following: • Failure of the patient to follow discharge instructions. This requires documentation that instructions were properly communicated to a patient or caregiver who was both not impaired and capable of following the instructions. • A condition caused by post-care services provided beyond the facility’s control. • A readmission after the patient left the same facility against medical advice.

extracted_content.title: Nonpreventable Readmissions
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Nonpreventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: Humana does not allow payment for the following types of readmissions since they are required to be reimbursed as part of the prior admission: • A planned readmission. • A readmission after a leave of absence. • A same-day related readmission.

extracted_content.title: Definitions of Italicized Terms
extracted_content.content: • Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) : Under IPPS, each inpatient admission is categorized into a case which is called a DRG. Each DRG has a payment weight assigned to it, based on the average resources used to treat Medicare patients in that DRG. • Same facility : Is an entity that owns or controls the facility for the first admission, an entity owned or controlled by the facility for the first admission, or an entity that is under common ownership or control as the facility for the first admission.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Definitions of Italicized Terms > Diagnosis Related Group (DRG)
extracted_content.content: Diagnosis Related Group (DRG): Under IPPS, each inpatient admission is categorized into a case which is called a DRG. Each DRG has a payment weight assigned to it, based on the average resources used to treat Medicare patients in that DRG. • Same facility : Is an entity that owns or controls the facility for the first admission, an entity owned or controlled by the facility for the first admission, or an entity that is under common ownership or control as the facility for the first admission.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s preventable subsequent observation stay review standards.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to facility services only. General Subsequent Observation Stay Review Requirements Observation stays following an inpatient admission at the same facility are subject to review to determine if the subsequent observation stay was preventable.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Subsequent Observation Stays
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Preventable Subsequent Observation Stays
extracted_content.content: If Humana determines that a subsequent observation stay was preventable, Humana does not allow payment for the subsequent observation stay . The following are examples of preventable subsequent observation stays . This is not an all-inclusive list: • Premature discharge from an inpatient admission that resulted in a subsequent observation stay . This is based on information that the provider or physician knew, or should have known, at the time of discharge. • Care rendered during the subsequent observation stay that should have occurred during the prior inpatient admission. • A subsequent observation stay that was not medically necessary. • A subsequent observation stay that is an attempt to circumvent Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) payment.

extracted_content.title: Separately Payable Subsequent Observation Stays
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Separately Payable Subsequent Observation Stays
extracted_content.content: If Humana determines that a subsequent observation stay was not preventable or was unrelated to the prior admission, Humana may allow separate payment for both the prior inpatient admission and the subsequent observation stay . The following are examples of subsequent observation stays that may be separately payable: • A subsequent observation stay that is due to a reoccurrence of a chronic condition and is not a continuation of the previous episode’s prior inpatient admission. • An unrelated subsequent observation stay , including an unrelated same-day subsequent observation stay . Facilities cannot be held responsible for subsequent observation stays beyond their control, which may include, but are not limited to, the following: • Failure of the patient to follow discharge instructions. This requires documentation that instructions were properly communicated to a patient or caregiver who was both not impaired and capable of following the instructions. • A condition caused by post-care services provided beyond the facility’s control. • A subsequent observation stay after the patient left the same facility against medical advice.

extracted_content.content: CPT code 77427 may only be submitted for five sessions , regardless of the actual time period in which the services were furnished. extracted_content.title: Units
extracted_content.content: The billing provider must submit each unit of five sessions as a distinct single-unit charge. For a three- session unit or four- session unit at the end of a course of treatment, the billing provider must submit a single-unit charge distinct from all other units. extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana reviews the higher-level office or other outpatient E/M services, CPT codes 99204, 99205, 99214 and 99215, to determine the level for reimbursement. extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s requirements and prohibitions for same-claim billing. Each statement outlined in this policy applies to both the reporting of reimbursable claims and the reporting of encounters, which are non-reimbursable claims for which the information is gathered for reporting.

extracted_content.title: Same-Claim Billing Requirements and Prohibitions When Applicable Regulatory Standards Exist
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.subsection: Same-Claim Billing Requirements and Prohibitions When Applicable Regulatory Standards Exist
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Same-Claim Billing Requirements and Prohibitions When Applicable Regulatory Standards Exist
extracted_content.content: When applicable regulatory standards exist establishing which services must be on the same claim and which services are not permitted to be on the same claim, Humana requires providers to comply with those standards.

extracted_content.title: Same-Claim Billing Requirements and Prohibitions When Applicable Regulatory Standards Do Not Exist
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.subsection: Same-Claim Billing Requirements and Prohibitions When Applicable Regulatory Standards Do Not Exist
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Same-Claim Billing Requirements and Prohibitions When Applicable Regulatory Standards Do Not Exist
extracted_content.content: Same-Claim Billing Requirements In the absence of applicable regulatory standards, Humana generally requires providers to submit all charges for the same encounter on one claim. Additionally, Humana generally requires a provider that submits a professional claim to report all charges for same-day services on that claim, regardless of whether they pertain to the same encounter . Exceptions: • When reference laboratory billing is acceptable, Humana permits a reference laboratory reporting charges for testing performed in distinct, specific service facility locations to submit a distinct claim for each service facility location. Note that this exception does not permit a reference laboratory to submit multiple claims for testing, that would otherwise be subject to a general requirement above, for the same service facility location. • Humana permits Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act (TEFRA) hospital interim claim billing, consistent with Original Medicare’s guidance on interim claim billing. Same-Claim Billing Prohibitions Apart from same-day professional-claim services, Humana generally does not permit a provider to report charges for services furnished in multiple encounters on the same claim. However, Humana also permits providers to report charges, on the same outpatient hospital claim, for repetitive services furnished in multiple encounters during the same calendar month.

extracted_content.content: At Humana’s sole discretion, Humana rejects, denies or recoups reimbursement for submissions that violate same-claim billing requirements and same-claim billing prohibitions, as outlined in this policy.

extracted_content.title: Timely Filing Alert
extracted_content.section: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy > Timely Filing Alert
extracted_content.content: Humana has established standards for determining whether reported charges meet applicable timely filing requirements, and those standards apply to all charges, including to charges reported on the same claim for services furnished in multiple encounters . For example, on a claim with charges for hospital outpatient repetitive services furnished during a month, Humana will deny a charge that was not submitted timely even if another repetitive services charge on that claim is timely and, therefore, potentially reimbursable.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: A colonoscopy allows the physician to examine the lining of the entire large intestine. It is most often used as a screening procedure to look for early signs of cancer in the colon or rectum. However, the test may reveal inflamed tissue, abnormal growths and ulcers. Special instruments can be passed through the colonoscope to remove any polyps if needed. In these cases, the screening colonoscopy results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. This policy describes Humana's billing expectation for distinguishing between a screening colonoscopy and a screening colonoscopy that results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana plans may allow screening colonoscopies and screening colonoscopies that result in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. Members and providers should contact Humana for specific plan information. • When billing screening services, healthcare providers must report an International Classification of Diseases (ICD) diagnosis code that accurately describes the screening . • If the service begins as a screening procedure but results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure at the same operative session, healthcare providers should report an appropriate screening ICD diagnosis code as the primary diagnosis and the diagnostic or abnormal finding ICD diagnosis code as the secondary or subsequent diagnosis. • When a screening results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure, as noted above, Humana will still allow the procedure as a screening if the following conditions are met: – The member has a screening colonoscopy benefit; – The claim contains both a screening and diagnostic diagnosis code and can be supported by medical records; and – The charge is not for a service performed more frequently than allowed, with respect to the previously allowed colorectal cancer screening , by Original Medicare guidelines. Healthcare providers should report modifiers PT and 33 when appropriate.

extracted_content.title: The following policy applies to only facility services.
extracted_content.subsection: The following policy applies to only facility services.
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > The following policy applies to only facility services.
extracted_content.content: Humana does not reimburse, under Medicare Advantage (MA) basic benefits, for self-administered drugs that are given in the outpatient hospital setting in the applicable jurisdiction. Self-administered drugs given in an outpatient hospital setting should be reported on hospital institutional claims using revenue code 0637 and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code A9270 . Drugs and biologicals given in an outpatient hospital setting that are not self-administered drugs should be reported using the combination of the applicable revenue code and applicable Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) or HCPCS code. A Humana MA member with Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage may be entitled to coverage of self-administered drugs by the Part D benefit carrier, and the enrollee may request reimbursement from that Part D benefit carrier.

extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for a short inpatient hospital stay .

extracted_content.title: Oklahoma Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. An inpatient claim billed for a short inpatient hospital stay is subject to review to determine the medical necessity of an inpatient level of care, based on Humana’s Short Inpatient Hospital Stay medical coverage policy, available in the References section of this policy. Humana requires the provider to submit medical records, when requested, for a short inpatient hospital stay. Humana may deny the claim if medical records are not received upon request. If Humana determines that medical necessity for the inpatient level of care was not met, according to Humana’s Short Inpatient Hospital Stay medical coverage policy, Humana denies the inpatient claim. Humana will accept an outpatient claim for the short inpatient hospital stay and will allow the provider to submit all service codes ordinarily appropriate for an outpatient level of care.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to only professional services. Humana does not separately reimburse a charge for a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II code assigned a payment status indicator of “B” on the MPFS Relative Value File . Humana considers reimbursement for status B codes to be included in the reimbursement for any other same-day charge. Exceptions : • Humana reimburses a charge for CPT code 90887, indicating a collateral outpatient therapy service, even though it is a status B code . • Humana reimburses a charge for CPT code 98960 , 98961 or 98962 when reported with modifier UB, indicating a service provided by a community health worker, even though they are status B codes . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, claims are subject to the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky out-of-network payment policy. For more information, see the relevant guidance in the References section of this policy.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Telehealth is a method of delivering healthcare services via electronic information and telecommunications technologies . Not all healthcare services delivered via electronic information and telecommunication technology are considered telehealth services. Examples of other healthcare services delivered via electronic information and telecommunications technologies that are not telehealth services include interprofessional services and remote monitoring services. The following policy outlines how Humana plans reimburse telehealth and other virtual services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to only professional services. This policy does not apply for services rendered during the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency (PHE). Note: Humana allows an originating site fee, reported by Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code Q3014 , to facilities that provide administrative support for a professional’s provision of a telehealth service if the patient is physically present at that facility. The originating site fee is not a telehealth service. The professional who provided the telehealth service is not eligible to receive reimbursement for the originating site fee in addition to the telehealth service provided.

extracted_content.title: Original Medicare Telehealth Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Original Medicare Telehealth Services
extracted_content.content: Humana requires a provider to submit a charge for an Original Medicare telehealth service according to the applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance for the date of service. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow Original Medicare telehealth services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. Humana MA plans deny charges for Original Medicare telehealth services that do not satisfy the applicable CMS guidance, including billing guidance regarding the appropriate place of service (POS) code or modifier, for the date of service. For further information on the service codes that may be reported as an Original Medicare telehealth service , see CMS’s List of Telehealth Services . Note: Humana MA plans have been applying the Congressionally-authorized, coverage-related waivers to Original Medicare telehealth services . These waivers expire December 31, 2027. Following CMS guidelines, Humana will apply the applicable limitations to a claim for a telehealth service beginning January 1, 2028, unless the service qualifies for coverage under the additional telehealth services benefit. For further information on the limitations that apply to Original Medicare telehealth service beginning January 1, 2028, see the CMS guidance available in the References section of this policy.

extracted_content.title: Additional Telehealth Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Additional Telehealth Services
extracted_content.content: For dates of service beginning January 1, 2020, Humana MA plans also allow certain additional telehealth services that are not Original Medicare telehealth services . Additional telehealth services must meet the following criteria: • The service must be one of those covered under the additional telehealth service benefit in the member’s applicable Evidence of Coverage. • The service must be provided by a physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner that has satisfied Humana’s telehealth credentialing and recredentialing standards and has a valid and effective contract with Humana. • The service must be provided by a physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner that satisfies the following requirements: – Meets all applicable licensure, certification and registration requirements, including Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) registration, if applicable, in the state(s) in which they practice and the state in which the patient is located at the time of the encounter; – Is operating within the scope of their license; and – Meets professional practice standards in the state(s) in which they practice and the state in which the patient is located at the time of the encounter. • The service must be provided using real-time interactive audio technology, and Humana encourages providers to simultaneously use real-time interactive video technology, when appropriate. For a charge for a particular service to be reimbursed, it must be possible to provide all the necessary components of the code with the real-time interactive technology used. • The physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner must verify the member’s identity before providing the service. • The Humana member must provide verbal or written consent to receive the service, in accordance with state law. • The Humana member must be present for the full duration of the service. Services not meeting the criteria outlined above will not be allowed by Humana as additional telehealth services . Unless prohibited by applicable federal statute or regulation, Humana plans allow additional telehealth services if it is medically appropriate to furnish the service via telecommunications-based technology, the service is coverable by the plan, and all applicable coding requirements are satisfied. For further information on the service codes that may be reported as additional telehealth services , see the Medicare Advantage Additional Telehealth Services Benefit Code List section of the policy. Physicians are responsible for supervising any additional telehealth services provided to Humana MA members by nonphysician practitioners within their practices to ensure that such services conform in all respects to the requirements set forth herein. Billing Place of Service Code Humana requires a provider report the POS code for an additional telehealth service as outlined below. For dates of service beginning January 1, 2024, a provider must report one of the following, as appropriate: • POS code 02 • POS code 10 • The applicable hospital POS code, if the patient is at home and the physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner is in the hospital, with modifier 93 or modifier 95 For dates of service from May 12, 2023, through December 31, 2023, a provider must report one of the following, as appropriate: • POS code 02 • POS code 10 • The POS code that would have been reported had the service been furnished in person with modifier 93 • The POS code that would have been reported had the service been furnished in person with modifier 95 Note : The POS code billed for a service will determine whether that service is reimbursed with a facility or nonfacility rate . Audio-Only Modifier Humana requires a provider to identify an audio-only service with modifier 93 . Medicare Advantage Additional Telehealth Services Benefit Code List The attached lists of procedure codes serve as a guide to assist providers in determining which services may be reimbursable under Humana’s MA additional telehealth services benefit. Click here* to view the attached code list for the applicable year.

Specific Requirements for Claims Submitted by Federally Qualified Health Centers and Rural Health Clinics A Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) or Rural Health Clinic (RHC) reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service , additional telehealth service , or other virtual service should follow the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. This also includes, but is not limited to, the following guidance for reporting the correct procedure code for the service: • An Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service that is a mental health service should be reported with the applicable HCPCS Level II or Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code for the service rendered. For the service to be allowed as an Original Medicare telehealth service , it must be on CMS’s List of Telehealth Services . For the service to be allowed as an additional telehealth service , it must be on the attached list of services that may be reimbursable under Humana’s additional telehealth services benefit for the applicable year. • An Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service that is not a mental health service should be reported with HCPCS code G2025 . • Another virtual service that is covered by Original Medicare but is not an Original Medicare telehealth service , as described above, should be reported according to the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. For dates of service through December 31, 2025, FQHC and RHC providers should report the virtual service with HCPCS code G0071 . For dates of service beginning January 1, 2026, FQHC and RHC providers should report the virtual service using the same service code as professional providers. In addition, FQHC and RHC providers should append modifier 95 when reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service .

extracted_content.title: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Time-based service codes are used by providers to document and bill for services that are measured and reimbursed according to the amount of time spent delivering the service. Examples include prolonged services and certain evaluation and management (E/M), therapy and care management services. Humana allows units for time-based service codes at the lesser of: • The limitation outlined in any applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) policy or guidance; • The limitation outlined in any applicable Kentucky Department for Medicaid Services (KDMS) policy or guidance; • The limitation outlined in any applicable Humana policy or guidance, including but not limited to, the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky Policies Booklet available in the References section of this policy; or • For each date of service, the maximum number of units that equals a single 24-hour period.

policy_title: Transition Period Billing for an Active Course of Treatment

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy provides information on billing for services furnished during a Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) member’s transition period and that are part of an active course of treatment that began before the member’s enrollment in the plan.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Pursuant to 42 C.F.R. § 422.112(b)(8)(i)(B), to prevent disruption of care, Humana does not require prior authorization for basic Medicare benefits during the first 90 days of a new member’s enrollment for active courses of treatment that started prior to

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: enrollment. Humana may review the services furnished during that active course of treatment against permissible coverage criteria when determining payment. To facilitate accurate claims processing of a service that, apart from the active course of treatment exception discussed above, would normally be subject to plan prior authorization requirements, Humana has developed optional modifier or condition codes. Use of these codes may facilitate claims processing by helping Humana identify claims related to an active course of treatment for new members. We encourage each provider to follow the guidance below when submitting claims for services furnished to new enrollees of Humana MA plans other than private fee-for-service (PFFS) plans: • For a professional claim , append modifier TZ to the code reported for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period . • For an outpatient facility claim , append modifier TZ to the code reported for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period . • For an inpatient facility claim , report condition code 9T for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period . A provider must not report the modifier or condition code discussed above to bill for a service: • If the service was not furnished as part of an active course of treatment that began before the member’s enrollment in the specific Humana MA plan; or • If the service was not furnished during that enrollment’s transition period ; or • If the service was furnished to a member of a Humana MA PFFS plan. In circumstances where a claim for a new member is submitted that may involve an active course of treatment but the provider did not append a modifier or condition code discussed above, Humana may evaluate medical record documentation included with the claim to determine whether the claim involved an active course of treatment . Note: Do not report the modifier or condition code discussed in this policy when submitting claims to Humana commercial or Humana Medicaid plans.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for transitional care management (TCM) services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana may reimburse one charge for professional TCM services per discharge if a patient requires case management when transferring from a facility setting to the community or home setting. Humana requires a provider to follow all TCM requirements as outlined in relevant Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined in this policy. Humana reimburses the first TCM charge received for the 30-day service period that meets all of the requirements outlined in this policy. A claim showing discharge from one of the following facility settings must be received to substantiate the necessity of the professional claim for TCM services: • Hospital outpatient observation or partial hospitalization • Inpatient acute care hospital • Inpatient psychiatric hospital • Inpatient rehabilitation facility • Long-term care hospital • Partial hospitalization at a community mental health center • Skilled nursing facility The services associated with the face-to-face portion of the professional TCM service must be rendered by a physician, which is limited to a medical doctor (MD) or doctor of osteopathic medicine (DO), or one of the following nonphysician practitioners (NPPs): nurse practitioner, physician assistant, clinical nurse specialist or certified nurse midwife. This includes behavioral health practitioners such as psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners. Any portions of the TCM service rendered by clinical staff must be provided under the general supervision of the billing physician or NPP and are subject to applicable state law, scope of practice requirements, and conditions for services and supplies furnished incident to the professional service of a physician or NPP. Clinical staff must meet the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1). A qualified health care provider may render TCM services for new or established patients; the reimbursement rate for TCM codes is the same regardless of new or established patient status. Note: Humana plans may reimburse a charge for reasonable and necessary evaluation and management (E/M) services for managing clinical issues, other than E/M services provided on the date of the required TCM face-to-face visit, in addition to a TCM charge, during the 30-day service period. Humana plans do not reimburse: • TCM services rendered by the surgeon during the postoperative period of a 10- or 90-day global surgery. • TCM services when discharge management services are provided by the same provider on the same day. • A TCM charge received after the first allowable TCM, whether from the same or different provider. • A TCM charge related to a discharge that occurs during the 29-day period after the date of an earlier discharge. • E/M services on the same date as the required TCM face-to-face visit when rendered by the same provider or group practice, regardless if an E/M modifier is reported.

policy_title: Z-Code® Billing for Molecular Diagnostic Testing

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Molecular Diagnostic Services (MolDX) program maintains a coding system of Diagnostics Exchange (DEX®) Z-Codes® that identifies a specific molecular diagnostic test. This policy establishes Humana’s requirements for Z-Code billing for molecular diagnostic testing.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires a provider to report a molecular diagnostic test with a unique DEX Z-Code, as assigned by MolDX, and the applicable Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II code. Humana denies a molecular diagnostic test CPT or HCPCS code when it is not reported with the applicable DEX Z-Code. Providers should contact the MolDX program to register molecular diagnostic tests.
